items.title: Flashpoint
items.text:
FRC robot telemetry: import WPILib .wpilog and CTRE .hoot logs, and track every motor's health across your robot's life. Runs offline on a pit laptop.

Replay puts one match on a timeline, with markers for heat, brownouts, stalls and CAN dropouts.

History follows each motor across every match, event and season. When the robot logs its CAN inventory, it tracks the physical motor by serial number through swaps.

Anomalies (beta) lists what looks wrong, with the evidence, for the team to triage.

Why Flashpoint says what it does for a team, and what it doesn't do yet.

Open the hosted demo: Replay in your browser, on real matches from team 6829's robots, with nothing to install.

items.title: Demo
items.text:
Look around Flashpoint's Replay view before you install anything:

Open the hosted demo

It's real data: seven matches from team 6829's (Ignite Robotics) 2025 and 2026 robots, from the Georgia district events. The header reads "Sample data · 6829" so you can tell it apart from your own.

items.title: What it is
items.text:
• Replay only. It's a static export (flashpoint report --static), the same thing you'd put on a USB stick. History, Anomalies, Setup and Live CAN need flashpoint serve, so they aren't in it.
  • No raw logs. The export leaves out the .wpilog and .hoot files, so there's nothing to download or open in AdvantageScope.
  • Nothing to set up. It runs in your browser and talks to no server but this site.

Start with Q7, Q73 and Q89 (2026, Georgia district championship): full qualification matches with tracks, markers and every motor in the readout. The seasons filter starts on the latest season; pick All seasons to see the 2025 matches.

The other four show what real logs can look like, and what Replay says about it: - E10: the robot code restarted during the match, so its Replay covers only the part before the restart. - P2 and Q30: wpilogs with no motor data to line up, marked no aligned samples. - Q19: hoots with no wpilog, also no aligned samples.

A match says "no aligned samples" explains each case.

items.title: FAQ
items.text: Short answers to the questions people ask most. The support matrix has the detail behind most of them.

items.title: Does it work with REV (Spark MAX, Spark Flex)?
items.text: Not yet. Flashpoint reads CTRE hoots and the WPILib wpilog, and has no reader for REV motor data, so REV motors get no Replay tracks, History or health. That's tracked in #108. A robot with a mix of CTRE and REV gets everything for its CTRE devices.

items.title: Does it work with AdvantageKit logs?
items.text: Not tested on real AdvantageKit logs yet. An AdvantageKit wpilog with Phoenix 6 hoots is the setup we expect to work, with match identity read from AdvantageKit's Driver Station fields (#76). See AdvantageKit, and if you can share a log, tell us.

items.title: We don't have Phoenix Pro. Is it still useful?
items.text: Yes. A hoot without Pro has every motor signal Flashpoint uses except temperature: current, voltage, velocity and CAN timing, so Replay, History, stall and brownout detection and CAN health all work. You lose temperature tracks and thermal findings. Phoenix Pro and temperature has the detail.

items.title: What about Systemcore and the 2027 season?
items.text: This version handles 2027's season file, and Flashpoint 0.3.1, planned for kickoff week (2027-01-16), adds what 2027 hoots and NetworkTables need: update then. Systemcore, the 2027 control system, hasn't been tested (#110). See Known limits.

items.title: Does it run on Windows?
items.text: Yes: install, ingest and serve are tested on Windows in CI, and the automatic import runs as a scheduled task. Windows gets the least real-world use of the three, so tell us what you hit. See Install on Windows.

items.title: What does it cost?
items.text: Nothing. Flashpoint is free and open source under the BSD 3-Clause license, made by FRC team 6829, Ignite Robotics. There's no paid tier and no account. Phoenix Pro is CTRE's license, and optional.

items.title: Where does our data live?
items.text:
On your laptop, in three folders: - the lake (~/flashpoint-lake by default): a copy of every log you import, and everything worked out from them; - the config folder (~/.config/flashpoint/, or %APPDATA%\flashpoint on Windows): your team, robot files and settings; - the cache (~/.cache/flashpoint/): the downloaded owlet converter.

Nothing is stored anywhere else unless you set up a backup, which copies the lake to a place you choose.

items.title: Does Flashpoint send our data anywhere?
items.text: No. There's no telemetry, no account and no server of ours. Flashpoint connects to other machines only for features you use: downloading owlet, pulling logs from your robot, your own backup, and Live CAN. Privacy and network lists each one.

items.title: Can several laptops share one lake?
items.text:
Not at the same time. Keep one laptop as the one that imports (the pit laptop), and let others look at it: - over the pit network, with flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0 (read-only for them); - with a Replay export on a USB stick; - or with a copy restored from the backup (Move to another laptop).

Don't put the lake in a folder that a sync tool (Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) shares between laptops that both write to it: the lake's ledger is a database file, and two writers can damage it.

items.title: How do we get help?
items.text: Ask in Q&A discussions: answers there stay searchable for the next team. Report bugs with the issue forms, and never attach match logs to a public issue (share them privately instead). Check Troubleshooting first.

items.title: What support can we expect during build season?
items.text: Flashpoint is maintained by volunteers on an FRC team, who are in build season too. From January to April, expect a first reply within a week; competition weekends are slower. See CONTRIBUTING.

items.title: Privacy and network
items.text:
Flashpoint runs on your laptop and sends no telemetry: no usage statistics, no crash reports, no account, and no server of ours. Everything it works out stays in your lake. This page lists every connection it makes, what your logs contain, and how to share them safely.

Checked by a test: with owlet already downloaded, ingesting, deriving, building Replay data and serving a match makes no connection beyond the laptop itself.

items.title: Every connection Flashpoint makes
items.text:
When To What goes over it The first time it reads a hoot of a new version CTRE's download server (redist.ctr-electronics.com), over HTTPS A download of the owlet converter. Nothing about you or your logs is sent. It's cached in ~/.cache/flashpoint/, so it happens once per hoot version (install offline avoids it) Robot pull (flashpoint acquire), only if you use it Your roboRIO (10.TE.AM.2, roborio-TEAM-frc.local or 172.22.11.2), over SSH and SFTP Listing and copying log files from the robot, and reading its free space. Flashpoint never deletes files on the robot Backup, only if you set backup.remote Wherever your rclone remote points (Google Drive, a NAS, another disk) A copy of the lake and your config folder, by rclone Live CAN, only while the view is open Your roboRIO, over NetworkTables Reading the CAN health topics robot code publishes You click a docs link in the app or doctor output The docs site (igniterobotics.github.io) An ordinary web page visit, in your browser

Installing and updating Flashpoint itself (with uv or pipx) downloads from PyPI; that's your package manager, not Flashpoint. The app's own pages, fonts and scripts are all served from your laptop.

items.title: What a log and a lake contain
items.text:
A wpilog holds whatever your robot code logs. Usually: - every NetworkTables value, including your own subsystem data and anything a vision coprocessor publishes; - Driver Station data: enabled, auto, teleop, and joystick inputs; - match data: event, match number and alliance station; - messages the robot program logs (DataLogManager.log()), and in recent WPILib versions its console output; - build info (project name, git branch), and with Flashpoint's samples the CAN inventory: every CTRE device's serial number.

A hoot holds each CTRE device's status signals, by CAN id and bus, including its firmware version.

The lake holds a copy of every raw log you imported, everything worked out from them, and your triage notes. Your team number and robot files are in the config folder.

None of that is secret in the usual sense, but it is your team's robot: your strategy code's NetworkTables values, your hardware list, and your match-by-match performance. Treat logs like your robot code.

items.title: Sharing logs for a bug report
items.text: Don't attach logs to a public GitHub issue or discussion. Say in the issue that you have logs to share, and a maintainer will reply with a private way to send them (Share logs privately). Logs shared with us are used only to test Flashpoint, and are deleted when you ask.

items.title: Showing the app on the pit network
items.text: flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0 lets other devices on the same network open the app. There's no password: anyone on that network who knows the laptop's address can see everything in the lake. The app is read-only then (for everyone, including the laptop itself), so nobody can change triage or settings, but they can read and download your logs. Only do it on a network you trust, and stop it (Ctrl-C) when you're done. See Show the app on the pit network.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text: From nothing to your own match in Replay: install, then three commands.

items.title: Your own logs
items.text:
You need a folder with one match's logs from your robot: the .wpilog from the roboRIO's USB stick or /home/lvuser/logs, and the .hoot files from CTRE signal logging. Then:

uv tool install --python 3.13 flashpoint
flashpoint init --team <your team number>
flashpoint ingest <your logs folder>
flashpoint serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and pick the match in Replay.

  • The install brings its own Python. If you don't have uv yet, or flashpoint isn't found afterwards, follow the Install page for your computer.
  • init asks for anything you leave out: your lake folder (where logs and results are stored), your team name and the app's colours.
  • The first ingest drafts your robot from the logs, so Replay shows motors straight away. Name each motor in Setup > Robots when you have a minute.
  • The first hoot downloads CTRE's converter, so do this once with internet before you rely on it at an event.

Stop the app with Ctrl-C.

items.title: Try it with sample logs
items.text:
No logs yet? Try Flashpoint on one real match from team 6829's 2026 season: qualification match 7 at the Georgia district championship, a full match with the robot enabled throughout. The bundle is 55.4 MB, with SHA-256 20ecfd9e3e4c8cdef14c26e80d75735cab048759e52565636a99987f79a8f96c.

It uses its own configuration and its own lake inside the bundle's folder, so your configuration and lake aren't touched. Install Flashpoint first (Install), then, in an empty folder:

macOS and LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
curl -LO https://github.com/IgniteRobotics/flashpoint/releases/download/samples-v1/flashpoint-sample-1.zip
echo "20ecfd9e3e4c8cdef14c26e80d75735cab048759e52565636a99987f79a8f96c  flashpoint-sample-1.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -
unzip -q flashpoint-sample-1.zip -d flashpoint-sample
cd flashpoint-sample
FLASHPOINT_CONFIG="$PWD/config" flashpoint ingest --lake "$PWD/lake" logs/
FLASHPOINT_CONFIG="$PWD/config" flashpoint serve --lake "$PWD/lake"

Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/IgniteRobotics/flashpoint/releases/download/samples-v1/flashpoint-sample-1.zip -OutFile flashpoint-sample-1.zip
(Get-FileHash flashpoint-sample-1.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq "20ecfd9e3e4c8cdef14c26e80d75735cab048759e52565636a99987f79a8f96c"
Expand-Archive flashpoint-sample-1.zip -DestinationPath flashpoint-sample
cd flashpoint-sample
$env:FLASHPOINT_CONFIG = "$PWD\config"
flashpoint ingest --lake "$PWD\lake" logs
flashpoint serve --lake "$PWD\lake"

The checksum line must print True. FLASHPOINT_CONFIG stays set in this PowerShell window, so close it when you're done; a new window uses your own configuration again.

The checksum line must print OK (on Windows, True). If it doesn't, the download was cut short: see The sample's checksum doesn't match.

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and pick 2026gacmp_qm7 in Replay. Anomalies has two findings from this match to look at. Stop the app with Ctrl-C.

Expected: a note about 10 declared signals

ingest prints one line about 10 declared signal(s) not written, naming CAN bus status signals such as can-rio-utilization. The sample's robot file is Ignite's, which declares the CAN bus status entries its robot code logs now; this match is from before that logger was added. Nothing is wrong with the sample.

To remove the sample, delete the flashpoint-sample folder.

Prefer to look around without installing anything? The hosted demo runs Replay on sample matches in your browser.

items.title: The 2027 season and Systemcore
items.text: This version ships a 2027 season file, so doctor stays green after January 1. But 2027 hoots will need a newer owlet than this version knows, and Live CAN's NetworkTables library is held below its 2027 release. Both come in Flashpoint 0.3.1, planned for kickoff week (2027-01-16): update then (Start a new season). Systemcore, the 2027 control system, is untested (#110). Season tracking: #73.

items.title: The first hoot needs internet
items.text: Flashpoint converts hoots with CTRE's owlet, which it downloads the first time it meets a hoot version and then keeps. A pit laptop that has never read a hoot can't read one offline. Ingest one hoot at home before the event, or install offline with owlet included. flashpoint doctor checks that the owlet for each hoot format in your lake is cached.

items.title: Hoots without a wpilog
items.text: A session with hoots but no wpilog gets no motor history: no Replay tracks, usage or match features. Ingest warns session(s) with hoots but no wpilog, and when every session of a season is like that, doctor's "Hoots without a wpilog" check warns too. One such session among many is usually the hoot logger restarting mid-event, and is safe to ignore. The fix is on the robot: turn on the WPILib DataLog. Hoot-only sessions are also missing from motor usage totals (#8).

items.title: Beta and experimental features
items.text: Feature Label Why Robot pull (automatic import from the robot) beta, tested on one robot Run on Ignite's robot only so far (#74). USB import has no label Anomalies beta Thresholds are tuned on one team's logs; expect findings to need judgement (#77) Live CAN experimental Needs robot code, and a fast bus can show false dropouts

items.title: Known issues
items.text: • Linux owlet can crash on power-loss-truncated hoots. On Linux, CTRE's owlet sometimes exits with an error on a hoot whose tail was cut off by a power loss (macOS doesn't). Flashpoint retries the conversion, so the file usually still imports with incomplete-read. If a hoot stays failed (owlet-failed), run flashpoint rebuild once. History: #4 (closed), tracked end to end in #71.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Fixes for the problems people hit in their first 30 minutes, by the message or symptom you see. Where Flashpoint prints the message, it's quoted exactly; <...> stands for the part that changes. For a bad key in a settings file, see that file's "Common errors" under Reference: config files. Still stuck? Ask in Q&A discussions, or see the FAQ.

items.title: flashpoint isn't found after installing
items.text:
What you see: flashpoint: command not found (macOS, Linux), or PowerShell saying flashpoint isn't recognized as the name of a cmdlet (Windows).

Why: uv tool install puts the command in uv's tool folder, which isn't on your PATH yet.

Fix: run uv tool update-shell, then open a new terminal window. If you installed with pipx, run pipx ensurepath instead. Check with flashpoint --version.

items.title: Python is refused
items.text:
What you see: pipx install flashpoint fails with pip saying the package requires a different Python, or flashpoint doctor shows a PROBLEM on Python:

Message: Python <version> isn't supported (3.11 to 3.14)

Why: Flashpoint runs on Python 3.11 to 3.14, and that install used another one.

Fix: install with uv, which downloads a supported Python for Flashpoint and leaves your own alone: uv tool install --python 3.13 flashpoint (Install). With pipx, point it at a supported Python: pipx install --python python3.13 flashpoint.

items.title: A proxy or firewall blocks the owlet download
items.text:
What you see: the first hoot fails to import. Ingest prints, with owlet-download-failed as the reason:

Message: FAILED <file>: failed (<reason>), will retry

and flashpoint doctor shows the owlet as not downloaded:

Message: owlet <version>: <state> (needed for the first hoot import; needs internet)

Why: Flashpoint converts hoots with CTRE's owlet tool, which it downloads from CTRE the first time it meets a hoot version. A school or event network can block that download.

Fix: any of these: - set your proxy for the command, for example HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example:8080 flashpoint ingest <folder> (PowerShell: $env:HTTPS_PROXY = "http://proxy.example:8080" first). Flashpoint uses the standard proxy variables; - ingest one hoot on another network (home, a phone hotspot) first: owlet stays cached in ~/.cache/flashpoint/ (or FLASHPOINT_CACHE), so it's needed only once per hoot version; - install offline, which brings owlet along.

The failed files are retried on the next ingest, so run it again once owlet can download.

items.title: Windows paths and quoting
items.text:
What you see: a command can't find a folder whose name has a space in it, a FLASHPOINT_CONFIG setting seems ignored, or a report.toml path turns into nonsense.

Why: PowerShell splits unquoted paths at spaces, sets environment variables differently from macOS and Linux, and TOML treats a backslash in double quotes as an escape.

Fix: - Quote paths with spaces: flashpoint ingest "D:\Robot Logs\GACMP", --lake "C:\Users\Pit Laptop\flashpoint-lake". - Set a variable with $env:, then run the command on its own line: $env:FLASHPOINT_CONFIG = "$PWD\flashpoint-sample\config". (set NAME=value is the old cmd.exe form, and the NAME=value command form is macOS and Linux only.) - In TOML files, write Windows paths in single quotes, so backslashes stay literal: path = 'C:\Users\Public\wpilib\2026\advantagescope\AdvantageScope (WPILib).exe'.

items.title: The sample's checksum doesn't match
items.text:
What you see: the Quickstart's checksum line for flashpoint-sample-1.zip prints FAILED (macOS and Linux) or False (Windows).

Why: the download was cut short or damaged.

Fix: delete flashpoint-sample-1.zip and download it again with the Quickstart's command, then check it again. If it still fails, report it with the bug form.

items.title: doctor problems
items.text: flashpoint doctor (and the Setup view) prints one line per check. Each PROBLEM line below is followed in the output by a fix: line with the command to run.

items.title: No configuration
items.text:
Message: no configuration in <folder>: Flashpoint doesn't know your team or robot

Why: there's no acquire.toml in the config folder, so Flashpoint has no team number and maps no robot.

Fix: flashpoint init --team <number>, or Create configuration in the Setup view.

items.title: No team number
items.text:
Message: no team number: no configuration yet

Message: no team number: acquire can't find your robot

Why: without a team number, robot pull can't work out the robot's addresses.

Fix: flashpoint init --team <number>, or set team in acquire.toml.

items.title: A settings file doesn't load
items.text:
Message: <file> doesn't load (see above)

or a line naming the file and its first bad key, such as robots/2026-comp.toml: slot.0.gearing: Extra inputs are not permitted.

Why: a typo, a key from another file, or a value of the wrong type. Flashpoint refuses unknown keys so typos don't pass silently.

Fix: edit the file the fix: line names. Each file's reference page lists its keys and its common errors: acquire.toml, robot files, theme.toml, report.toml, anomaly.toml, season files.

items.title: No robot for this season
items.text:
Message: no robot configured for season <year>, and the lake has <year> logs: their motors aren't matched to slots

Why: the lake has logs from this season but no robot file says which motor is which.

Fix: use Draft robot in the Setup view, or let the next flashpoint ingest draft one (Set up a robot file). Then run flashpoint derive.

items.title: The lake folder can't be written
items.text:
Message: can't write to <folder>

Message: can't create <folder>: <parent> isn't writable

Fix: point lake in acquire.toml (or --lake) at a folder you own, such as ~/flashpoint-lake.

items.title: Hoots this version can't read
items.text:
Message: the lake has C<number> hoots, which this Flashpoint can't read

Why: a newer Phoenix version writes a hoot format (its "compliancy") this Flashpoint has no owlet for. This happens after a new season's Phoenix release.

Fix: update Flashpoint (Update Flashpoint), then run flashpoint rebuild --quarantined to read the hoots that were set aside.

items.title: owlet isn't downloaded, or its checksum doesn't match
items.text:
Message: owlet <version>: <state>

where the state is not downloaded or checksum doesn't match. It's a PROBLEM when the lake already has hoots that need it.

Fix: flashpoint ingest of any hoot downloads it again (with internet). If the checksum keeps failing, delete ~/.cache/flashpoint/owlet/ and ingest again. Behind a proxy, see above.

Message: owlet <version> has no build for <platform>

Why: CTRE doesn't publish owlet for this computer's operating system and processor (for example 32-bit Windows).

Fix: import hoots on a supported computer (support matrix).

items.title: The backup is overdue
items.text:
Message: <what> not backed up for <time> (<last backup>)

Message: rclone isn't installed, so no backup can run; <status>

Why: logs or configuration have waited longer than backup.overdue_h hours for a backup, or rclone, which does the copying, isn't installed.

Fix: install rclone if the message says so, then flashpoint backup once you're online. To quiet it over a long event with no internet, raise overdue_h (Back up the lake).

items.title: AdvantageScope path not found
items.text:
Message: configured AdvantageScope path not found: <path>

Fix: correct path under [advantagescope] in report.toml, or clear it to use the WPILib install. The Setup view's Set AdvantageScope path button does it for you.

items.title: Replay says "No Replay data"
items.text:
Replay shows No Replay data with one of three explanations.

Message: The lake holds no imported logs yet: <lake>

Why: nothing has been imported into the lake the app is reading. Often the logs went into a different lake: ingest and serve each use --lake, else FLASHPOINT_LAKE, else lake in acquire.toml, else ~/flashpoint-lake.

Fix: import with the command the view shows, or run serve with the same --lake you imported into. If it also says files were quarantined, see A file was quarantined.

Message: Replay lists only competition matches, identified from FMS data in the log or a match-style log file name.

Why: every log in the lake is practice, pit or home testing, not a competition match. See Every log is a non-match session.

Message: <count> waiting for Replay data. On the laptop that holds the lake, run:

Why: the matches are imported, but their Replay data hasn't been built. The automatic import builds it; a plain ingest builds it too, unless it was run with --no-derive.

Fix: flashpoint report. For one match the view names, flashpoint report --match <key>.

items.title: Ingest says derive failed
items.text:
What you see: ingest or rebuild lists the imported files, then an error from derive, then:

Message: derive failed: Replay data was not built. Fix the error above, then run: flashpoint derive --report

Why: the files were imported, but the derive that runs after the import stopped with an error, so no Replay data was built for them. The error printed just above says why; a broken robot file shows as robot configuration error. The command exits 1 even when every file imported. Running ingest again doesn't help: it skips files it already has, so derive doesn't run again.

Fix: fix the error derive printed (for a robot file, see A settings file doesn't load), then run flashpoint derive --report.

items.title: Every log is a non-match session
items.text:
What you see: Replay lists no matches, and History shows the logs' motor usage.

Why: Flashpoint names a match from the FMS info in the log, then from the file name (FRC_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_<event>_<match>.wpilog), then from The Blue Alliance. A log from practice, the pit or home has none of those, so it's a non-match session. That's expected away from an event. At an event, the Driver Station gets FMS info only when connected to the field.

Fix: nothing, for practice logs: History still counts their usage. If they really are matches, keep the original file names (WPILib names them with the event and match once the FMS connects), and make sure robot code records NetworkTables to the DataLog, where the FMS info arrives.

items.title: A match says "no aligned samples"
items.text:
What you see: the match list shows NO ALIGNED SAMPLES, and the match opens with the reason in place of its tracks:

Message: No aligned samples: there is no wpilog to align its hoots to.

Fix: robot code needs to write a wpilog as well as hoots: turn on the WPILib DataLog. The match's raw hoots are still listed for download.

Message: No aligned samples: no robot is configured for robot code <project> in season <year>, so its devices aren't matched to slots. Add one with Draft robot in the Setup view.

Fix: see The robot shows as "unknown".

Message: No aligned samples: no device data could be aligned to the wpilog.

Why: the hoots and the wpilog share no signal or enable edge Flashpoint can line up (how alignment works).

Fix: open the match in AdvantageScope from the same view to look at the raw logs, and report it with the bug form if both logs look complete.

items.title: The robot shows as "unknown"
items.text:
What you see: matches show robot "unknown", and their motors aren't mapped to slots.

Why: no robot file matches the log. Either the log's season has no robot file, or it has several (a practice and a competition bot) and none has the project the robot code logged in its build info.

Fix: use Draft robot in the Setup view on one of the logs (Set up a robot file), or set project in the right robot file to the log's project name. Then run flashpoint derive.

items.title: Replay shows "Low alignment confidence"
items.text:
Message: ▲ Low alignment confidence (<method>): hoot and wpilog times may disagree. Check events against AdvantageScope.

Why: the hoots were lined up by the robot-enable edges or the wall clock, not by a signal written to both logs, so times can be off by up to half a second.

Fix: treat marker times as approximate. Robot code that writes one signal to both logs (CTRE's swerve code does) gets exact alignment.

items.title: No temperature
items.text:
What you see: Replay's header names the buses without temperature:

Message: Temperature not logged on <buses>: the hoots are not Pro-licensed, and temperature needs a Phoenix Pro-licensed device on that bus.

and those buses' temperature cells read not logged (needs Phoenix Pro). A gyro or CANcoder reads temperature not tracked, Pro or not. When no bus has temperature and every hoot was Pro-licensed, the header says instead:

Message: Temperature not logged. <reason>

with the reason:

Message: No temperature was logged for this match.

Why: a hoot exports motor temperature only when that bus's log has a Phoenix Pro-licensed device. The second message means the hoots had Pro but no temperature signal was recorded.

Fix: see Phoenix Pro and temperature. Everything except temperature works without Pro. flashpoint doctor shows how many of your hoots are Pro-licensed.

items.title: A file was quarantined
items.text:
What you see: ingest lists the file as quarantined, with a reason such as empty-file:

Message: QUARANTINED <file>: <reason>

Why: the file itself is bad, so Flashpoint sets it aside instead of retrying it. The reason says how:

Reason Means empty-file The file is 0 bytes: the robot lost power before writing anything invalid-header Not a wpilog or hoot, or damaged at the start too-old A wpilog version older than Flashpoint reads unsupported-version A wpilog version newer than Flashpoint reads unsupported-compliancy:<n> A hoot format this Flashpoint has no owlet for: update no-signals-for-profile The hoot has none of the signals Flashpoint reads

A file whose conversion keeps failing (owlet-failed, owlet-timeout) is quarantined after its third try. Quarantined files are listed by flashpoint doctor; they're never shown in the app.

Fix: usually none: an empty or damaged file has nothing to read. For unsupported-compliancy, update Flashpoint and run flashpoint rebuild --quarantined, which tries every quarantined file again. A later ingest skips the file, saying it was quarantined earlier.

items.title: A file was imported as incomplete
items.text:
What you see: ingest imports the file with a warning, short-coverage or incomplete-read; when you open the match in AdvantageScope from Replay, the hoot is listed with an INCOMPLETE badge:

Message: WARNING <file>: <warning>

Why: - short-coverage: the hoot covers much less time than the other hoots of its session, usually because it was cut short. - incomplete-read: owlet read what it could and stopped early, because the file's end is missing. That's what a robot power-off mid-write leaves behind.

Fix: none needed: Flashpoint keeps what was read. The missing stretch has no data, and Replay shows it as not logged. If a hoot that should be complete keeps doing this, check the robot's disk space.

items.title: User guide
items.text: For students and mentors who run Flashpoint: at the pit, after an event, or on the team laptop. You don't need to know Python. If you want to change the code, read the developer guide instead.

items.title: What Flashpoint is for
items.text:
Flashpoint keeps every robot log the team records and tracks the health of each motor over the robot's whole life. It reads: - WPILib DataLogs (.wpilog), which the roboRIO writes every time the robot runs; - CTRE Phoenix 6 signal logs (.hoot), one per CAN bus, with motor current, voltage, temperature, and CAN health.

From those it answers questions like: - Which motor ran hottest in Q7, and when? - Is the front-left drive motor drawing more current than it did last month? - Did we brown out, and which part of the match was it? - Which motor keeps losing CAN frames when its neighbours don't?

It flags problems (anomalies) before they cost a match, and it follows each physical motor by its serial number, so a motor's history stays with it when it moves to another slot or robot.

Everything runs on one laptop with no internet.

What it isn't: - It isn't a live dashboard; it reads logs after the robot is off. - It isn't a replacement for AdvantageScope. For a deep look at one log (every signal, field view, odometry), Flashpoint opens the log in AdvantageScope for you.

items.title: Install
items.text:
You need a computer running one of: - macOS 13 or later; - Linux with glibc 2.35 or later (Ubuntu 22.04 or later); - Windows on an x86-64 PC (not Windows on ARM).

Flashpoint runs on Python 3.11 to 3.14 (not 3.15 yet). You don't have to install that Python yourself: uv downloads one for Flashpoint if your computer doesn't have a suitable one.

  1. Install uv, once. On macOS, brew install uv. On Windows, winget install --id=astral-sh.uv -e. On Linux (or any of them), use uv's installer. Open a new terminal afterwards.
  2. Install Flashpoint and create your configuration:

uv tool install --python 3.13 flashpoint
flashpoint init --team 1234
3. Import one match's logs, then look at them:

flashpoint ingest path/to/one-match/
flashpoint serve

If flashpoint isn't found after the install, run uv tool update-shell and open a new terminal.

With pipx instead. If you already use pipx, it works too, but it needs a Python 3.11 to 3.14 already installed: - macOS and Linux: pipx install --python python3.13 flashpoint (any of python3.11 to python3.14 that you have). - Windows: in the python.org installer, tick "py launcher". Then py -3.13 -m pip install --user pipx, and py -3.13 -m pipx install flashpoint.

flashpoint init creates your config folder (~/.config/flashpoint, or %APPDATA%\flashpoint on Windows) with your team number, your lake folder, your team name and colours (theme.toml), and copies of the default settings. Anything you leave out (--team, --lake, --team-name, --palette) it asks for in a terminal; leave the name blank for none. See flashpoint init for the options. It never overwrites a file, so running it again is safe. The robot addresses Flashpoint tries come from the team number.

Your first import drafts your robot. When the lake has logs from a season that has no robot file yet, ingest drafts one from them (robots/2026-comp.toml, from the match with the most CAN devices) and says so. Replay shows that match's data right away. Open Setup > Robots and fill in each slot's subsystem and role; keep the drafted slot ids, which already name each device's model and CAN id. Logs with hoots but no wpilog, or an import with --no-robot-draft, draft nothing: use Setup > Draft robot for those (Setup).

flashpoint doctor lists the setup checks. Right after init, the robot check is a warning: the lake has no logs from this season yet. Once you import this season's logs it is a problem only while no robot is configured. A drafted robot whose slots have no subsystem yet is a warning, not a problem.

items.title: Updating
items.text: See Update Flashpoint.

items.title: Installing without internet
items.text: See Install without internet.

items.title: Installing from a checkout
items.text:
For Ignite's own laptops, or to try changes that aren't released yet, install from the repository:

git clone https://github.com/IgniteRobotics/flashpoint.git
cd flashpoint
uv tool install --python 3.13 .

Ignite's configuration (robots, units, failure labels) is the checkout's config/ folder. Point Flashpoint at it in your shell profile (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc), or copy it to ~/.config/flashpoint:

export FLASHPOINT_CONFIG="$HOME/flashpoint/config"

On Windows, set it once with setx FLASHPOINT_CONFIG "%USERPROFILE%\flashpoint\config", then open a new terminal. To update a checkout install: git pull, then uv tool install --force --python 3.13 ..

items.title: Before an event: get ready offline
items.text:
Hoot files are converted with CTRE's owlet tool. Flashpoint downloads the right owlet version the first time it sees a hoot of that format, so ingest one recent hoot while you still have internet:

flashpoint ingest path/to/a/recent.hoot
flashpoint doctor

doctor checks owlet for each hoot format in your lake: each must say downloaded, verified. With no hoots yet, it checks the newest owlet this version of Flashpoint knows. In the Setup view, Download owlet does the same without a hoot.

That newest owlet may be last season's. If CTRE changes the hoot format for a new season, only a Flashpoint update can read the new hoots, and doctor can't tell until it sees one. So ingest a hoot from this season's robot code before an event (see Starting a new season).

items.title: Where your data lives: the lake
items.text:
Flashpoint keeps everything in one folder, the lake, at ~/flashpoint-lake by default. To use another folder, such as a bigger drive, use one of these. When more than one is set, the first in this list wins: 1. --lake PATH on any command; 2. FLASHPOINT_LAKE in your shell profile; 3. lake in acquire.toml in your config folder (flashpoint init --lake PATH does this).

A leftover FLASHPOINT_LAKE hides what acquire.toml says. flashpoint doctor shows the lake in use.

The lake keeps an untouched copy of every log, so you can delete the copies you imported from. Don't edit files inside the lake by hand. How it works explains what each folder holds.

items.title: Import logs by hand
items.text:
Copy logs off the robot or a USB stick into any folder, then:

flashpoint ingest path/to/logs/

You can pass files or folders, and folders are searched all the way down. A file that's already in the lake is skipped, so running it twice is fine.

At the end, ingest prints a summary like this:

  WARNING     GACMP_E10_rio_2026-04-11_19-29-15.hoot: incomplete-read
  QUARANTINED GADAL_Q11_..._2026-03-06_17-52-51.hoot: empty-file
  FAILED      GACMP_Q7_rio_2026-04-09_21-51-06.hoot: failed (owlet-download-failed), will retry
13 ingested, 0 skipped, 1 failed, 1 quarantined, 0 quarantined earlier in 13.1s
  • Ingested files are in the lake.
  • WARNING means the file was read but something was off. incomplete-read means the end of the file is missing, usually because the robot lost power while writing it. The rest of the data is still used.
  • QUARANTINED means the file is bad: it's empty, corrupt, or in a format Flashpoint can't read. It's kept in the lake but not used, and later runs don't try it again. They list it as quarantined earlier.
  • FAILED means the laptop failed, not the file. Usually there was no internet to download owlet, the tool that reads .hoot files. Run flashpoint ingest again once you're online, or let automatic import retry it. If owlet crashes on the same file 3 times, the file is quarantined.
  • To retry quarantined files, for example after updating Flashpoint, run flashpoint rebuild --quarantined. It works from the lake's own copies, so you don't need the original logs.
  • "declared signal(s) not written" lines mean the robot config expects a NetworkTables entry that the log doesn't have, which is normal for older code. It only matters if you were looking for that signal.
  • "session(s) with hoots but no wpilog" means some hoots had no .wpilog from the same time to align to. Their motors get no history: no Replay charts, usage or match features. Motor history needs both files, the hoots from Phoenix 6 and a wpilog from WPILib data logging (DataLogManager.start() in robotInit()). One such session among many is usually the hoot logger restarting mid-event, and is safe to ignore. When every session of a season is like this, doctor's "Hoots without a wpilog" check warns too: the robot code isn't writing wpilogs.

Ingest then works out matches, aligns the logs, runs anomaly detection, and updates Replay, all on its own.

items.title: How matches are identified
items.text:
Replay lists competition matches only. Flashpoint knows a log is from a match when: 1. the wpilog holds FMS data (FMSInfo), which the robot gets from the field at an event; or 2. the wpilog's file name has the match in it, the way the Driver Station names match logs: FRC_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_EVENT_Q7.wpilog (P for practice, Q for qualification, E for elimination matches).

Logs from the shop, the practice field or the pit have neither, so they get no Replay entry. They still count in History: every motor's usage, temperatures and anomalies include them. When Replay is empty but the lake has logs, it says how many sessions it found that aren't matches.

To have logs pulled from the robot and USB sticks without doing this by hand, set up automatic import.

items.title: Look at the data: flashpoint serve
items.text:
flashpoint serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in a browser. Stop the server with Ctrl-C. The app has these views.

Each view has its own reference page, with every control, marker and badge:

View For Replay One match: tracks, markers, a readout of every motor, and the raw logs History Every motor over time, one point per match Anomalies (beta) What detection flagged, with evidence, likely causes and triage Setup The doctor checks, your whole configuration, and Draft robot Live CAN (experimental) CAN dropouts while you shake-test or drive-test

items.title: Showing other people on the pit network
items.text: See Show the app on the pit network. There's no password, and the app is read-only over the network.

items.title: Take Replay on a USB stick
items.text: See Take Replay on a USB stick.

items.title: Team name and colours
items.text: The app header shows your team name and number, and the app uses your team's colours. Both live in theme.toml: see Set the team name and colours and the theme.toml reference.

items.title: Describe a robot
items.text:
Flashpoint needs to know which motor is which. Each robot has a file in the robots/ folder of your config folder. The quickest start is Draft robot in the Setup view. Every key, NetworkTables signals, sibling groups, the battery proxy, swap dates and which robot file a log uses are in the robot file reference.

The other settings files (report.toml, anomaly.toml, anomaly-causes.toml, failure-labels.toml, seasons/, units/units-seed.csv) each have a page under Reference: config files. A file missing from your config folder uses the default that ships with Flashpoint.

items.title: Starting a new season
items.text: See Start a new season.

items.title: Check the setup: flashpoint doctor
items.text:
Run flashpoint doctor whenever something looks wrong. It changes nothing.

Section What to look for lake The folder you expect, and how many files are at each stage. "N file(s) from an older pipeline version" means a Flashpoint update needs flashpoint rebuild config The config folder in use. "missing" means run flashpoint init (or set FLASHPOINT_CONFIG for a checkout's config/) defaults Settings files that come from the defaults shipped with Flashpoint, because your config folder has no copy seasons, robots Each season's roots and each robot. An empty robot list means no robot file was added yet checks One line per setup check. PROBLEM lines say what's wrong and the fix under them; doctor then exits 1. See the CLI reference owlet cache Where owlet is kept. The owlet check says whether each version your logs need is downloaded; if not, you can't convert hoots offline acquire The last automatic import and backup (automatic import) AdvantageScope Which install "Open in AdvantageScope" uses

items.title: Event-day checklist
items.text:
The week before: - [ ] First event of a season? Do Starting a new season first. - [ ] Update Flashpoint (Updating) while you have internet, and run flashpoint doctor. - [ ] Make sure this season's owlet is downloaded: Download owlet in Setup, or ingest a recent hoot. - [ ] Confirm the robot in Setup matches the robot: CAN IDs, swaps since last event. - [ ] If you use automatic import, run flashpoint acquire --dry-run with the robot on.

At the event: - [ ] After each match, pull logs: automatic import, or copy them and run flashpoint ingest. - [ ] flashpoint serve and check Replay for FAULT markers, and Anomalies for anything new. - [ ] Triage what you looked at, so the queue stays meaningful.

After the event: - [ ] Back up the lake (backup). - [ ] Add any real failures to failure-labels.toml in your config folder.

items.title: Why Flashpoint
items.text:
Every FRC season has these three stories: - The motor that died in eliminations. It had been running hotter for weeks, and the logs show it, but nobody had time to graph forty matches. - The CAN dropout nobody could find. A device falls off the bus for a few hundred milliseconds, the mechanism twitches, and by the time anyone looks, the robot is fine. - The brownout in autonomous. The robot stops for half a second in auto, and the drive team swears they didn't touch anything.

Your robot already recorded what happened in each of them. Flashpoint reads those logs, keeps every match, and shows you each motor's health across the robot's whole life.

items.title: It follows the motor, not the CAN ID
items.text: When a motor is swapped onto another mechanism, or moved to the practice robot, its history goes with it. Flashpoint follows each physical motor by its CTRE serial number, when robot code logs its CAN inventory. Without the inventory, it follows each position on the robot (a slot), and you mark swap dates in the robot file. How it works has the details.

items.title: It keeps the robot's whole life
items.text: History puts every match in the lake on one chart: peak temperature, supply current, energy, stall time or CAN gaps, one line per motor, across matches, events and seasons. A motor that runs hotter than it used to, or draws more than its twin on the other side of the drivetrain, stands out. Temperature needs Phoenix Pro on the device; current and CAN gaps don't. See the History view.

items.title: It shows each match on one timeline
items.text: Replay lines up battery voltage, current and temperature for one match, with a marker wherever a rule fired: temperature limits, brownouts and sags, stalls, device reboots, CAN dropouts, and whole-bus gaps. Click a marker to see the motor and the moment. Brownouts are judged on a battery proxy (the supply voltage the CTRE devices report), because Flashpoint doesn't read the PDH or PDP yet. See the Replay view.

items.title: It flags anomalies (beta), with the evidence
items.text: Anomaly detection (beta) checks each match against fixed limits, each motor's own history, and its siblings (the four drive motors, say). It flags a match over a temperature limit or with a brownout, a metric that creeps away from its usual value over several matches or jumps and stays there (such as a loosening connector raising supply path resistance), and a motor that leaves its sibling group. Each anomaly (beta) comes with its evidence and a list of likely causes to check, and the team triages it: someone is looking into it, it's fixed, or it's expected. The note is shown next time the same thing turns up on that motor. Detection is tuned on one team's robots so far, so treat a finding (beta) as a reason to check, not a verdict. See Triage an anomaly (beta).

items.title: It finds loose CAN connectors in the pit (Live CAN, experimental)
items.text: Live CAN (experimental) watches the robot while you shake-test it: wiggle each harness and see which device drops out, reboots or faults, and whether it was one device or the whole bus. It needs a small publisher in robot code, and it can show false dropouts on a fast bus. See Live CAN health (experimental).

items.title: It runs offline on a pit laptop
items.text: No account, no server of ours, and no telemetry. Once the converter for your hoots is downloaded, Flashpoint makes no connection beyond the laptop, and a test checks that. Privacy and network lists every connection it can make. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows (Install).

items.title: It reads the logs you already record
items.text: Turn on CTRE signal logging (.hoot) and the WPILib DataLog (.wpilog), and Flashpoint has what it needs. A few extra lines of robot code (the CAN inventory, CAN bus status) let it do more; Robot side says what each one adds, with Java samples that compile.

items.title: It opens AdvantageScope instead of replacing it
items.text: When you need every frame of one log, Replay's OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE opens the match's wpilog there, with the hoots in the same folder. Flashpoint is for the view across matches; AdvantageScope is for the deep dive. See Open a match in AdvantageScope.

items.title: It's free and open source
items.text: BSD 3-Clause (license). Built by FRC team 6829, Ignite Robotics, and open to contributions.

items.title: What it doesn't do (yet)
items.text:
• REV and Phoenix 5 devices aren't supported. Flashpoint reads Phoenix 6 devices from their hoots (#108 tracks REV, #109 Phoenix 5).
  • No PDH or PDP. Battery voltage comes from a proxy (#6).
  • No temperature without Phoenix Pro. Free hoots don't carry it (#75).
  • Hoots alone give no motor history. A session needs its wpilog too (Hoots without a wpilog).
  • Tested on one team's robots. AdvantageKit logs, other teams' wiring and devices Ignite doesn't run read "not tested" until someone's logs show them working.
  • 2027 and Systemcore need a later version; see The 2027 season and Systemcore.

The support matrix lists every device, log setup and platform with how it was tested, and Known limits has the rest.

items.title: See it for yourself
items.text:
• The hosted demo is Replay in your browser, on real matches from team 6829's robots. Nothing to install.
  • The Quickstart installs Flashpoint and gets your own match into Replay with three commands, or tries it on a sample match first.

items.title: Import logs from the robot automatically
items.text:
Beta: beta, tested on one robot. Pulling logs from the robot, and running the watch as a service, have been checked on one team's roboRIO so far. Importing from USB sticks isn't affected. If a pull misbehaves on your robot, please open an issue.

flashpoint acquire --watch pulls new logs into Flashpoint without anyone copying files. Leave it running on the pit laptop, or on a team computer the robot connects to:

  • When the robot is powered and on the same network, it pulls the new logs.
  • When someone plugs a USB stick into the laptop, it copies the logs off that too.

Each new log is ingested, derived, checked for anomalies, and built into Replay within a cycle or two.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• Flashpoint installed, and a configuration with your team number:

    uv tool install --python 3.13 flashpoint
flashpoint init --team <your team number>

    The Install page has the steps for each computer. The robot addresses Flashpoint tries come from the team number. - The robot on, and this computer on its network: the radio, Ethernet, or the USB tether. - Robot code that writes its logs to /home/lvuser/logs or the robot's USB stick (Signal logging). - To run it as a background service: Linux or Windows. On macOS, you leave it running in a terminal.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Check what it would copy, with the robot on. This changes nothing:

    flashpoint acquire --dry-run

    robot 10.68.29.2: ok, 2 to copy
  10.68.29.2  /home/lvuser/logs/FRC_20260409_215113_GACMP_Q7.wpilog  20563712 bytes
  ...
dry run: 2 file(s), 41127424 bytes would be copied; nothing changed

    robot: unreachable means no address answered (see Troubleshooting). To try another address for one run, add --host <address>.

  2. Run one real cycle. It copies the new logs, checks each copy, and ingests them:

    flashpoint acquire

  3. Leave it running:

    flashpoint acquire --watch

    Stop it with Ctrl-C. To have it start on its own, run it in the background.

  4. Set up a backup, so the logs it pulls don't exist only on this laptop (Back up the lake). The watch then backs up on its own.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Check it worked
items.text:
Run flashpoint doctor. Its acquire section shows the last cycle and each source with its result (ok, unreachable or error) and what it copied. The pulled matches are in Replay after you reload the page. Check the status lists everything the section can show.

Each cycle of the watch ends with a log line like this:

cycle done: robot 10.68.29.2 ok, volume ROBOT-USB ok; transfers 3 verified; inbox 3 success

If a source is unreachable or a file failed to copy, see the table below. For files that fail to import, see Troubleshooting.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: What it does
items.text:
Every cycle (default every 30 seconds) the watch does the following, in order:

  1. Robot: it tries each configured robot address until one answers, then lists the .wpilog and .hoot files in the log folders on the roboRIO (internal storage and its USB stick). New files are copied over SFTP into the lake's inbox/. Each copy is checked against the size and SHA-256 hash of the file on the robot.
  2. USB drives: it looks for removable drives plugged into this computer, finds .wpilog and .hoot files up to four folders deep, and copies the new ones with the same checks. When a drive is finished, the log says volume <name> (<path>) is safe to remove.
  3. Ingest: everything in inbox/ is ingested, then derived, then run through detection. This includes files you drop in inbox/ by hand.
  4. Replay: after a successful derive, it builds the Replay data for the new or changed matches only (the same build as flashpoint report). A running flashpoint serve lists a new match in Replay after you reload the page; you don't need to restart it. A build that fails, or that finds another build already running, is tried again next cycle, also after the watch restarts.
  5. Backup: if a backup is configured and due, it runs.

It never changes anything on the robot or the stick. It doesn't delete, move, or rename anything there, and it has no option to.

A file is pulled once. The pull history lives in the lake, so restarting the watch, or plugging the same stick in again, copies only what's new.

Files still being written are skipped. On the robot, the newest .wpilog in each folder and the newest hoot session are still open while the robot code runs. The watch leaves them and pulls them on a later cycle, after the robot code restarts or the robot is power-cycled. Files that change while being listed are also left for the next cycle. To take open files anyway, run flashpoint acquire --include-active once. Those copies are tagged as incomplete reads.

WPILib and Phoenix start deleting old logs when the robot's disk gets close to full. When a log folder on the robot has less than low_space_mb free (default 100 MB), the watch logs a warning, and doctor shows it. Pull the logs and clear space on the robot by hand before it starts deleting them (Disk space).

Importing from cloud folders (Google Drive, Dropbox, network shares) isn't supported. Download those files and use flashpoint ingest (Import logs from a USB stick), or drop them in <lake>/inbox/.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Configure it: acquire.toml
items.text:
flashpoint init writes acquire.toml in the config folder (~/.config/flashpoint/, %APPDATA%\flashpoint on Windows, or the FLASHPOINT_CONFIG folder) with your team number and lake. Without a team number or hosts, acquire refuses to start and names flashpoint init. Unknown keys are an error, so typos are caught. Every key, its default and what it does is in the acquire.toml reference.

The watch reads acquire.toml once, when it starts. After you change it, here or in the Setup view's Team and connection section, restart the watch: systemctl --user restart flashpoint-acquire on Linux, schtasks /End then schtasks /Run /TN flashpoint-acquire on Windows, or Ctrl-C and start it again.

The first time the watch connects to a robot, it records the robot's SSH key in ~/.cache/flashpoint/known-robots.json. If the key changes later (the rio was reimaged), it logs a warning and accepts the new one.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Run it in the background
items.text:
Beta: beta, tested on one robot. Running acquire as a service has been checked on one team's setup so far.

The easiest way is the Setup view: its acquire service check has an Install button on Linux and Windows. To do it by hand, clone the repository to get the service files, then run the commands below from that folder:

git clone https://github.com/IgniteRobotics/flashpoint.git
cd flashpoint
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Linux (systemd user service)
items.text:
Flashpoint ships a unit file, src/flashpoint/deploy/systemd/flashpoint-acquire.service. It expects flashpoint at ~/.local/bin/flashpoint, which is where uv tool install and pipx put it.

  1. Install and start it:

    mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp src/flashpoint/deploy/systemd/flashpoint-acquire.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now flashpoint-acquire
journalctl --user -u flashpoint-acquire -f      # watch its log

  2. If you set FLASHPOINT_CONFIG or FLASHPOINT_LAKE in your shell profile, put them in ~/.config/flashpoint/env too, one KEY=value per line. Services don't read your shell profile:

    FLASHPOINT_CONFIG=/home/pit/flashpoint/config

  3. On a computer with no one logged in, keep the service running after logout:

    loginctl enable-linger "$USER"

  4. On a computer with no desktop, the watch only sees USB drives that are mounted. Install udisks2 and udiskie, and run udiskie as a user service (systemctl --user enable --now udiskie), so drives mount when plugged in.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Windows (scheduled task)
items.text:
Flashpoint ships a task definition, src/flashpoint/deploy/windows/flashpoint-acquire.xml. It runs %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\flashpoint.exe acquire --watch at logon, restarts it up to 3 times if it fails, and never runs two copies at once. From the cloned folder:

schtasks /Create /XML src\flashpoint\deploy\windows\flashpoint-acquire.xml /TN flashpoint-acquire
schtasks /Run /TN flashpoint-acquire

The task uses your user environment, so it sees FLASHPOINT_CONFIG if you set it with setx (only needed for a checkout install; flashpoint init doesn't need it). To remove it: schtasks /Delete /TN flashpoint-acquire /F.

Ending the task (schtasks /End, or End in Task Scheduler) kills it immediately. A copy cut off mid-file leaves a .part file in the inbox, which is never ingested and is cleaned up on the next start.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: macOS
items.text:
There's no service definition for macOS yet. Run the watch in a terminal window and leave it open:

flashpoint acquire --watch

To keep it running after you close the terminal, use tmux (brew install tmux): run tmux, start the watch, then press Ctrl-B then D to detach. Run tmux attach to get back to it. Stop it with Ctrl-C either way.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Backup and restore
items.text: The watch also backs up the lake's raw logs, its metadata and your configuration to an rclone remote, such as Google Drive, every interval_min minutes. Set backup.remote in acquire.toml to turn it on. Back up the lake covers setting it up, what a backup holds, when a backup is overdue, and the restore drill.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Check the status
items.text:
flashpoint doctor

The acquire section shows:

  • the last cycle;
  • each source with its result (ok, unreachable, error) and what it copied;
  • low-space warnings;
  • files that failed to copy, with the reason;
  • whether derive is pending or failed;
  • whether a Replay build is owed (Replay build pending) or failed (Replay build error: ..., with the end of its output);
  • the last backup.

On Linux, journalctl --user -u flashpoint-acquire has the full log. verified copies in the cycle done line passed the hash check, and size-verified copies were checked by size only. retry copies failed and will be tried again next cycle.
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
These are the problems specific to pulling logs. For problems importing the files once they're copied, see Troubleshooting.

You see What it means What to do robot: unreachable in the dry run, or unreachable in doctor None of hosts answered. That's normal when the robot is off, and the watch keeps trying Check that the robot is on and this computer is on its network (radio or USB tether). Try flashpoint acquire --dry-run --host 10.68.29.2. Check team in acquire.toml robot <host>: cannot open a session: ... The robot answered but SSH login failed Check user and password in acquire.toml A USB stick is plugged in but nothing is copied The drive isn't seen as removable, isn't mounted, or has no logs within four folders of its top Make sure the drive shows up in Finder, File Explorer, or lsblk. On a Linux computer with no desktop, set up udiskie. Check that removable_media isn't false removable volume detection failed, followed by the error The operating system's drive listing failed It retries next cycle. If it repeats, run the watch in a terminal to see the full error The newest log on the robot isn't pulled It's still open, and the watch skips open files Restart the robot code or power-cycle the robot, or run flashpoint acquire --include-active once robot <host>: low space on <root>: N MB free The robot is close to deleting old logs on its own Pull the logs, then free space on the rio robot <host> has no sha256sum; files are accepted on size The rio image is missing a tool, so copies are checked by size only Safe to ignore; size checks still catch truncated copies another acquire is running on this lake (pid ... on ... since ...) Another acquire, or a backup, is using this lake Stop the other one, or let it finish. If that process has already exited, just run again: the lock is released automatically, so there is never a stale lock to delete A .part file in inbox/ A copy was cut off because the watch was killed, or the computer lost power, partway through. (A stick pulled mid-copy removes its own .part and counts as a failed try.) Nothing. .part files are never ingested and are removed on the next start ingest exited with N and changed nothing; inbox kept Ingest failed on something in the inbox Run flashpoint ingest <lake>/inbox by hand to see the error Replay build error: ... in doctor The Replay build after derive failed; the watch tries again every cycle Run flashpoint report by hand to see the full error. Usually a mistake in a robot file (robots/ in your config folder) or in report.toml. flashpoint doctor shows where your config folder is a Replay build is already running on this lake from flashpoint report The watch (or another report) is building Replay data right now Run it again once that build ends; there is never a stale lock to delete failed ... lines in doctor A file failed its copy check three times, and the watch has stopped retrying it Copy it by hand and run flashpoint ingest on it; if that fails too, the file on the robot is damaged
path: Import logs from the robot automatically

items.title: Back up the lake
items.text:
The lake is the only copy of your imported logs and your anomaly triage. Back it up off the laptop, along with your configuration, and practise a restore before you need one.

Flashpoint backs up with rclone to any remote rclone supports, such as Google Drive, a NAS or another disk. Flashpoint never reads your rclone credentials.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• Flashpoint installed and configured, with at least one log imported. On an empty lake, flashpoint backup stops with no ledger at <lake>/meta/flashpoint.sqlite; nothing to back up.
  • rclone installed: follow rclone's install page.
  • Somewhere to back up to, and internet (or a network) to reach it.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Make an rclone remote, once. rclone config asks a few questions; give the remote a short name, such as gdrive:

    rclone config

  2. Open acquire.toml in your config folder (~/.config/flashpoint/ on macOS and Linux, %APPDATA%\flashpoint on Windows) and add the remote, with a folder on it:

    [backup]
remote = "gdrive:flashpoint"

    interval_min and overdue_h go in the same table. They're in the acquire.toml reference.

  3. Run one backup now:

    flashpoint backup

    It prints what it backed up:

    backed up raw, metadata and configuration to gdrive:flashpoint

    A large first backup can take a while. If automatic import is running, this command exits with code 3 and says a running watch backs up on its own: the watch does it instead.

  4. Leave the backups to the watch. flashpoint acquire --watch backs up every interval_min minutes (default 15) when something changed, such as a new log or a saved robot file or threshold. Without the watch, run flashpoint backup after each import.

  5. Run the restore drill once, so you know the backup works.

items.title: Check it worked
items.text:
flashpoint doctor (or the Backup check in the Setup view) says when the last backup succeeded:

  ok       Backup                       last backup 3 min ago

The remote has three folders, raw, meta and config:

rclone lsd gdrive:flashpoint

If the check is a warning or a problem, see The backup is overdue.

items.title: What a backup holds
items.text:
• Raw logs, copied once and never overwritten.
  • Metadata, including anomaly triage: a consistent snapshot in meta/latest on the remote. Each backup moves the files it replaces into meta/history/<UTC time>/, so a backup from a wrong or empty lake can't destroy the last good one. Nothing deletes old history folders; remove them by hand when you want the space.
  • Your configuration, in config/latest: the TOML files at the top of the config folder and in seasons/ and robots/, and the CSV files in units/. Nothing else in that folder is copied: not the service's env file, not the Setup view's .backups/, not notes you left there. flashpoint init puts copies of the default files in the folder, so they're backed up too, even if you never changed them. Each backup moves the files it replaces or deletes into config/history/<UTC time>/.

Bronze, silver, gold and the Replay data aren't backed up: they're rebuilt from raw.

Within the watch, each backup gives up on a dead connection within about a minute and stops after 4 minutes. A large first backup goes up over several cycles, and doctor shows the backup as still owed until it's done.

To get an older robot file back, copy it from the history with rclone:

rclone copy gdrive:flashpoint/config/history/20261023T180000Z/robots/2026-comp.toml ~/.config/flashpoint/robots/

items.title: When a backup is overdue
items.text:
The Backup check, in flashpoint doctor and the Setup view, watches for data that exists only on this laptop:

  • A log is waiting when the lake received it after the last successful backup. Your configuration is waiting when it changed since then. This works the same whether logs came in through the watch or flashpoint ingest.
  • Problem: something has waited longer than backup.overdue_h hours (default 24). The message says how many logs, whether configuration changed, for how long, and the last error, for example 2 logs and configuration changes not backed up for 30 h (last backup 2 days ago). The Setup tab shows a ! in your warning colour on every view until a backup succeeds. doctor exits 1.
  • Warning: the last backup failed, but nothing has waited that long yet. Also when backup.remote is set but rclone isn't installed: rclone isn't installed, so no backup can run; <status>.
  • ok: says when the last backup succeeded. With no backup.remote set, it's ok and marked (optional), and says how many logs exist only on this laptop.

The check only reads what's recorded on this laptop; it never contacts the remote. At an event without internet, it turns into a problem after a day. That's accurate: nothing from the event is backed up yet. Once you're back online, the watch catches up on its own, or run flashpoint backup. To keep it quiet over a long event, raise overdue_h (for example 72). Before going back to a Flashpoint version older than this one, remove the overdue_h line: older versions refuse unknown keys.

items.title: Restore drill
items.text:
Practise this before you need it. Always restore into a new lake folder and an empty config folder, never over the ones you're using. Pointing FLASHPOINT_CONFIG at a new folder makes the drill act like a new laptop.

  1. Restore into a scratch lake and a scratch config folder, then rebuild:

    macOS and LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
    export FLASHPOINT_CONFIG=~/restore-drill-config
flashpoint restore --remote gdrive:flashpoint --lake ~/restore-drill
flashpoint rebuild --lake ~/restore-drill

    $env:FLASHPOINT_CONFIG = "$HOME\restore-drill-config"
flashpoint restore --remote gdrive:flashpoint --lake "$HOME\restore-drill"
flashpoint rebuild --lake "$HOME\restore-drill"

    --remote is needed because the new config folder has no acquire.toml yet. restore prints:

    restored 47 file(s) from gdrive:flashpoint; bronze, silver and gold must be rebuilt
restored the configuration into /home/pit/restore-drill-config
run: flashpoint rebuild

    The rebuild converts every hoot again, so it takes a while, and needs owlet (internet, if this laptop has never downloaded it).

  2. Check the restored lake:

    macOS and LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
    flashpoint doctor --lake ~/restore-drill

    flashpoint doctor --lake "$HOME\restore-drill"

    The lake section counts the files, and the robot and owlet checks are ok. To look at it, run flashpoint serve --lake ~/restore-drill and check that Replay lists your matches and Anomalies keeps your triage.

  3. Go back to your own configuration, then delete the two scratch folders:

    macOS and LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
    unset FLASHPOINT_CONFIG

    Remove-Item Env:FLASHPOINT_CONFIG

What restore does and doesn't do:

  • It copies the raw logs and metadata, including anomaly triage. It refuses a lake that already has data (<lake>/meta/flashpoint.sqlite already exists; restore into a new lake, or pass --force). Use a new lake rather than --force.
  • It copies your configuration into the config folder only if that folder has no configuration files yet. If it has any, nothing in it is changed: the backed-up copy goes to restored-config/ inside the restored lake, and restore says kept the configuration in <config folder>; the backed-up copy is in <lake>/restored-config. Compare and copy what you need by hand. --force never changes this.
  • A backup made before configuration was included still restores; restore says the backup held no configuration.
  • To restore an older metadata snapshot, first copy that meta/history/<time>/ folder over meta/latest on the remote with rclone.

The full options are in the CLI reference. To move to a new laptop for real, see Move Flashpoint to another laptop.

items.title: Import logs from a USB stick
items.text: Copy the robot's logs off its USB stick, or off the roboRIO itself, and import them into the lake. To have this happen on its own, see Import logs from the robot automatically.
path: Import logs from a USB stick

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• Flashpoint installed, and a configuration made with flashpoint init (Install).
  • Internet the first time you import a hoot, so Flashpoint can download owlet, CTRE's hoot converter. After that, importing works offline (Before an event: get ready offline).
  • Robot code that writes its logs where you'll look. DataLogManager.start() writes the wpilog to a logs folder on the robot's USB stick when one is plugged in, and to /home/lvuser/logs otherwise (DataLog). Signal logging puts the hoots next to it.
path: Import logs from a USB stick

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Turn the robot off, then take the USB stick out of the roboRIO and plug it into the laptop.

    No stick, or the logs are on the rio's own storage? Copy them over SFTP instead, with the robot on and the laptop on its network. The user is lvuser, with no password unless your rio has one. For team 6829 the address is 10.68.29.2 (10.TE.AM.2):

    scp -r lvuser@10.68.29.2:/home/lvuser/logs ~/robot-logs

    An SFTP app such as WinSCP or FileZilla works too. Then go to step 3.

  2. Copy the stick's logs folder to the laptop in Finder or File Explorer, for example into a folder called robot-logs in your home folder. Then the stick can go back in the robot. Each robot power-on writes its own files; copy them all. Files already in the lake are skipped later, so copying old ones again does no harm.

  3. Import the folder:

    macOS and LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
    flashpoint ingest ~/robot-logs

    flashpoint ingest "$HOME\robot-logs"

    You can pass files or folders, and folders are searched all the way down. Quote a path with a space in it.

  4. Read the summary at the end. Files that need attention are listed first, then one line counts them:

      WARNING     GACMP_E10_rio_2026-04-11_19-29-15.hoot: incomplete-read
  QUARANTINED GADAL_Q11_..._2026-03-06_17-52-51.hoot: empty-file
  FAILED      GACMP_Q7_rio_2026-04-09_21-51-06.hoot: failed (owlet-download-failed), will retry
13 ingested, 0 skipped, 1 failed, 1 quarantined, 0 quarantined earlier in 13.1s
    • WARNING: the file was read, but something was off. incomplete-read means its end is missing, usually because the robot lost power while writing it. The rest is used.
    • QUARANTINED: the file is bad (empty, damaged, or a format Flashpoint can't read). It's kept in the lake but not used, and later imports don't try it again.
    • FAILED: the laptop failed, not the file, usually because owlet couldn't be downloaded. Run the same command again once you're online.

    The exit code is 1 when a file failed or was quarantined in this run.

  5. Wait for the rest. After the import, ingest works out the matches, maps the motors to your robot file, runs anomaly detection and builds the Replay data, each with its own line:

    derived 4 of 4 session(s)
detected 0 anomalies (0 HIGH, 0 MED, 0 LOW); 22 unit(s) building baseline; scanned through 2026gacmp_qm7
built 4, unchanged 0, removed 0; 4 match(es) listed in 2.1s

    The first import of a season also drafts your robot file (Set up a robot file).

  6. Look at the matches:

    flashpoint serve

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/. Stop the app with Ctrl-C.

You can delete the copies on the laptop afterwards: the lake keeps an untouched copy of every log.
path: Import logs from a USB stick

items.title: Check it worked
items.text:
The summary's first count is the number of files ingested. Replay lists each competition match by its key, such as 2026gacmp_qm7. Replay lists matches only: a log is a match when it holds FMS data from the field, or its file name has the match in it, the way the Driver Station names match logs (FRC_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_EVENT_Q7.wpilog). Logs from the shop, the practice field or the pit get no Replay entry, but History counts their motor usage (How matches are identified).

report prints a line when some sessions had no match key:

  3 session(s) without a match key (no Replay entry; their usage still counts in History)

If Replay is empty, see Replay says "No Replay data" and Every log is a non-match session. For lines in the summary, see A file was quarantined, A file was imported as incomplete, and, for owlet-download-failed, A proxy or firewall blocks the owlet download.
path: Import logs from a USB stick

items.title: Install without internet
items.text: Prepare one folder on a computer with internet, carry it on a USB stick, and install Flashpoint from it on a pit laptop that never goes online. The folder holds everything the install and the first hoot import would otherwise download: Flashpoint and its dependencies, a Python, uv, the owlet hoot converter, and these docs.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• An online computer with the same operating system and processor as the pit laptop: an Apple silicon or Intel Mac, a Linux x86-64 PC, or a Windows x86-64 PC. On macOS and Linux, uname -m prints arm64 or x86_64. Python and uv are built for one system, so a folder made on a Mac won't install on Windows.
  • uv on the online computer (Install), and Flashpoint installed there too, to download owlet.
  • One hoot from each season your logs come from, such as last season's and this season's robot code. Each season's Phoenix release can use a new hoot format, and each format needs its own owlet.
  • A USB stick with about 1 GB free. The folder is about 300 MB.

This page uses Python 3.13, the version the normal install uses.

items.title: Collect the folder (on the online computer)
items.text:
Every command runs from the folder that will hold flashpoint-offline, such as your home folder. On Windows, run them in PowerShell.

  1. Make the folder:

    mkdir -p flashpoint-offline/wheels

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force flashpoint-offline\wheels

  2. Download Flashpoint and every dependency it needs, as wheels for the pit laptop's system and Python 3.13. Use the line for the pit laptop:

    macOS, Apple silicon:

    uvx --python 3.13 pip download --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.13 --platform macosx_13_0_arm64 flashpoint -d flashpoint-offline/wheels

    macOS, Intel:

    uvx --python 3.13 pip download --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.13 --platform macosx_13_0_x86_64 flashpoint -d flashpoint-offline/wheels

    Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.35 or later; pip needs each tag listed):

    uvx --python 3.13 pip download --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.13 --platform manylinux_2_35_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_34_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 flashpoint -d flashpoint-offline/wheels

    Windows x86-64:

    uvx --python 3.13 pip download --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.13 --platform win_amd64 flashpoint -d flashpoint-offline\wheels

    It ends with Successfully downloaded flashpoint and the names of the other packages. Every dependency has wheels for these systems, so nothing needs building. For Flashpoint 0.2.0 that's 27 files.

  3. Download Python 3.13 for the pit laptop, and pack uv's copy of it:

    uv python install 3.13
(cd "$(uv python dir)" && tar -czf "$OLDPWD/flashpoint-offline/python.tar.gz" cpython-3.13.*)

    uv python install 3.13
Compress-Archive -Path "$(uv python dir)\cpython-3.13.*" -DestinationPath flashpoint-offline\python.zip

  4. Download uv for the pit laptop. Use the line for the pit laptop:

    # macOS, Apple silicon
curl -L -o flashpoint-offline/uv.tar.gz https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
# macOS, Intel
curl -L -o flashpoint-offline/uv.tar.gz https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
# Linux x86-64
curl -L -o flashpoint-offline/uv.tar.gz https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz

    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip -OutFile flashpoint-offline\uv.zip

  5. Download owlet for each hoot format your logs use, by importing one hoot of each season into a scratch lake. Then pack the owlet cache:

    flashpoint ingest --lake <scratch folder> <last season's .hoot> <this season's .hoot>
tar -czf flashpoint-offline/owlet.tar.gz -C ~/.cache/flashpoint owlet

    flashpoint ingest --lake <scratch folder> <last season's .hoot> <this season's .hoot>
Compress-Archive -Path "$HOME\.cache\flashpoint\owlet" -DestinationPath flashpoint-offline\owlet.zip

    If you set FLASHPOINT_CACHE, pack the owlet folder in there instead. flashpoint doctor prints the folder on its owlet cache line. The cache holds one file per hoot format, named owlet-<version>-C<format> (with .exe on Windows):

    Season Hoot format File 2024 C6 owlet-1.0.1.1-C6 2025 C13 owlet-25.4.1-C13 2026 C19 owlet-26.3.0-C19

    These are the versions Flashpoint 0.2.0 uses. Delete the scratch lake afterwards.

  6. Download the docs for your version: flashpoint-docs-X.Y.zip from the version's GitHub Release, into flashpoint-offline.

  7. Copy flashpoint-offline to the USB stick.
