roots = ["/home/lvuser/logs", "/u/logs"]
poll_s = 30
settle_s = 5
low_space_mb = 100
removable_media = true

[backup]
remote = "gdrive:flashpoint"
interval_min = 15
overdue_h = 24
Key Default What it does team none Your team number, 1 to 99999. Robot pull tries 10.TE.AM.2 (team 6829: 10.68.29.2, team 254: 10.2.54.2), then roborio-TEAM-frc.local, then the USB tether 172.22.11.2 lake ~/flashpoint-lake The lake folder for every command. --lake and FLASHPOINT_LAKE override it. A relative path is taken from the folder the command runs in, not the config folder, so give the acquire service an absolute path: it runs from a different folder than your shell. init and the Setup view always write an absolute path hosts [] (use the team's addresses) Robot addresses to try instead, in order. --host ADDR replaces it for one run user lvuser SSH user on the roboRIO password "" (none) SSH password, if the rio has one roots /home/lvuser/logs, /u/logs Log folders on the robot, searched with their subfolders: internal storage, and the robot's USB stick poll_s 30 Seconds between cycles in --watch settle_s 5 Seconds to wait and re-check a file's size before copying it, so half-written files are skipped low_space_mb 100 Warn when a robot log folder has less free space than this (Disk space) removable_media true Scan USB drives plugged into this computer. --no-usb turns it off for one run backup none The [backup] table. Without it, nothing is backed up remote none (no backup) In [backup]: the rclone remote and path, such as gdrive:flashpoint (Back up the lake) interval_min 15 In [backup]: minutes between backups in --watch overdue_h 24 In [backup]: hours logs or configuration may wait for a backup before the backup check reports a problem. At least 1

The watch reads acquire.toml once, when it starts. After changing it, restart the watch (Import logs from the robot automatically).

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
flashpoint doctor checks the file and names the key. These are its messages:

  • A misspelt key (here tem for team): 
    acquire.toml: tem: Extra inputs are not permitted
  • A number in quotes: 
    acquire.toml: team: Input should be a valid integer
  • A value out of range: 
    acquire.toml: backup.overdue_h: Input should be greater than or equal to 1
  • A key given twice: 
    acquire.toml: Cannot overwrite a value (at line 3, column 12)

items.title: anomaly-causes.toml
items.text:
anomaly-causes.toml holds the "likely causes" shown with each anomaly: suggestions to check, never a diagnosis. Flashpoint ships a starting list. Copy it to your config folder and add what you found each time you resolve an anomaly, so the next student sees it.

[[cause]]
method = "SPEC"
metric = "reboots"
text = "Loose power lug or connector"

[[cause]]
method = "STEP"
metric = "stator_current_p95"
subsystem = "intake"
text = "Something rubbing or jammed in the intake"

Each [[cause]] table:

Key Required What it is method yes SPEC, DRIFT, STEP, SIBLING or MODEL metric yes The metric, as anomaly.toml's metrics names it, or reboots, longest_gap_ms, brownouts or feature_vector (MODEL) subsystem no Only for slots in this subsystem. These entries are listed first text yes The cause, up to 300 characters

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
From flashpoint doctor:

  • A cause with no text: 
    anomaly-causes.toml: text: Field required

items.title: anomaly.toml
items.text:
anomaly.toml sets how anomaly detection judges each motor. The values and their defaults are in the bundled default, with a comment on each; copy it to your config folder to change one. Unknown keys are rejected. After an edit, run flashpoint detect; you don't need to re-derive.

The five methods are described in How it works. Each table below belongs to one of them.

items.title: [spec]: fixed limits
items.text:
Judged per match, and shown at every sensitivity.

Key Finding temp_max_med_c Match maximum temperature at or above this: MED temp_max_high_c ... HIGH temp_mean_med_c Match mean temperature: MED stall_med_s Stall time in a match: MED gap_med_ms Longest isolated CAN gap: MED gap_high_ms ... HIGH brownout_high This many brownouts in a match (same rule as Replay's FAULT marker): HIGH

Reboots have no key: any reboot while enabled is HIGH, any other is MED.

items.title: [baseline]: DRIFT and STEP
items.text:
Each motor against its own history (median and MAD of its last matches).

Key What it sets metrics The metrics judged against the motor's history window How many previous matches make the baseline min_baseline Fewer prior matches than this: "building baseline", no DRIFT or STEP step_z STEP: the last step_persist matches all beyond this z, same sign step_persist ... for this many matches drift_z DRIFT: the median of the last drift_span matches beyond this z drift_span ... over this many matches med_z Severity: MED at |z| of at least this high_z ... HIGH at least this; below med_z, LOW floors The [baseline.floors] table: the smallest spread per metric, so a very steady history can't make every change huge

items.title: [sibling]: SIBLING
items.text:
Each motor against the median of its sibling group.

Key What it sets z How far from the group's median counts need Flagged in at least this many ... of ... of the last this-many matches the whole group played

items.title: [strict]: the strict sensitivity
items.text:
Extra findings at lower thresholds, shown when the Anomalies view's sensitivity is strict. Each must be at or below the normal value.

Key Instead of step_z [baseline] step_z drift_z [baseline] drift_z sibling_z [sibling] z persist [baseline] step_persist

items.title: [model]: MODEL (off by default)
items.text:
An isolation forest over each motor's match features. It needs the optional ml extra installed.

Key What it sets enabled Turn it on contamination The share of scores to flag (0.01 is the top 1 %) min_train Motor-matches needed before it scores anything

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
From flashpoint doctor:

  • A value that isn't a number: 
    anomaly.toml: baseline.step_z: Input should be a valid number, unable to parse string as a number

items.title: failure-labels.toml
items.text:
failure-labels.toml records real failures and repairs, so flashpoint backtest can check whether detection caught them, and how early. There's no default: you write it as things break. Ignite's is config/failure-labels.toml.

A label is caught when an anomaly on its motor (and metric, when given) is open at its match, or within the 5 matches before it.

[[label]]
robot = "2026-comp"
slot = "intake-roller"
match = "2026johnson_qm105"
kind = "failure"
metric = "reboots"
note = "Intake roller leader rebooted while enabled after an 820 ms CAN dropout."

Each [[label]] table:

Key Required What it is robot yes A robot file's robot name unit a unit or a slot The motor: a serial (ctre:<serial>) or a legacy unit id slot a unit or a slot A slot id on that robot, or power for brownouts match a match or a date A match key like 2026gacmp_qm7 date a match or a date YYYY-MM-DD, for a failure outside a match kind yes failure, degradation or repair note yes What happened metric no Only an anomaly on this metric counts

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
From flashpoint doctor:

  • A kind that isn't one of the three: 
    failure-labels.toml: kind: Input should be 'failure', 'degradation' or 'repair'
  • A robot with no robot file: 
    failure-labels.toml: label 1: unknown robot 'x'

items.title: report.toml
items.text: report.toml sets the limits behind Replay's rule markers, History's health badges and the charts' reference lines, and where to find AdvantageScope. Most teams never change it. The values and their defaults are in the bundled default; copy it to your config folder to change one. Unknown keys are an error. After an edit, run flashpoint report (or let the watch do it) to rebuild Replay data.

items.title: [thresholds]
items.text:
Key Used for temp_warn_c Motor temperature for a WARN marker, History's WARN health, and the temperature reference line temp_fault_c Temperature for a FAULT marker and History's HOT health brownout_v The battery proxy below this voltage ... brownout_hold_s ... for at least this long is a brownout: a FAULT marker sag_v The battery proxy below this voltage: a WARN marker voltage_danger_v History's minimum-voltage reference line sample_gap_s A whole CAN bus silent this long during the match: WARN dropout_warn_s One device's CAN frames stopping this long while others still talk: WARN. At least the event floor Flashpoint keeps gaps from gap_limit_s How long one battery proxy sample can count as low, at most, before the next

The battery proxy is the robot file's battery_proxy slot, or else the median supply voltage across devices. Detection has its own limits, in anomaly.toml.

items.title: [advantagescope]
items.text:
Key Used for path The AdvantageScope program to open matches in. Empty (the default) uses the newest WPILib install, then a standalone install. On Windows, use single quotes so backslashes stay literal: path = 'C:\Users\Public\wpilib\2026\advantagescope\AdvantageScope (WPILib).exe'

See Open a match in AdvantageScope.

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
From flashpoint doctor:

  • A misspelt threshold: 
    report.toml: unknown keys ['temp_warn']

items.title: Robot files (robots/*.toml)
items.text:
A robot file tells Flashpoint which motor is which: every CAN device on the robot (a slot), what the robot code calls its buses, the NetworkTables signals to bring in, which slots to compare with each other, and which device stands in for the battery. Each robot has one file in the robots/ folder of your config folder, such as Ignite's 2026-comp.toml.

The quickest start is Draft robot in the Setup view, which writes one from a log (Set up a robot file). Your first import usually drafts one for you.

items.title: A whole file
items.text:
Most slots are left out here; the sibling group names three drive slots that aren't shown.

robot = "2026-comp"        # keep it the same as the file name: robots/2026-comp.toml
season = 2026
project = "Robot-2026"     # the robot code's project name, from build info
battery_proxy = "gyro"     # optional: a slot id

[[slot]]
id = "drive-fl"
bus = "canivore"
model = "TalonFX"
can_id = 11
subsystem = "drivetrain"
role = "front-left drive"
gear_ratio = 6.746031746031747
swaps = [2026-03-02]       # optional: dates this motor was replaced, for logs with no CAN inventory

[[slot]]
id = "gyro"
bus = "canivore"
model = "Pigeon2"
can_id = 1
subsystem = "drivetrain"
role = "gyro"

[[bus]]                    # optional: the robot code's name for a bus, tied to its hoot bus
name = "DriveTrain"
hoot = "canivore"

[[signal]]                 # optional: a NetworkTables or wpilog value to bring in
id = "intake-at-extension-setpoint"
root = "robot"
entry = "Intake/At Extension Setpoint"
subsystem = "intake"
metric = "at_setpoint"

[[siblings]]               # optional: slots that do the same job, compared with each other
name = "drive"
slots = ["drive-fl", "drive-fr", "drive-bl", "drive-br"]

items.title: Top level
items.text: Key Required What it does robot yes The robot's name. Keep it the same as the file name season yes The season (calendar year) this file is for project yes The robot code's project name, as its build info logs it. Picks this file when a season has more than one robot battery_proxy no A slot id whose supply voltage stands in for the battery (below) slot yes The [[slot]] tables, one per CAN device bus no The [[bus]] tables signal no The [[signal]] tables siblings no The [[siblings]] tables

items.title: [[slot]]: one CAN device
items.text: Key Required What it does id yes A short name, unique in the file, such as drive-fl bus yes rio, canivore (any CANivore), or a CANivore's 32-character hex id when the robot has more than one model yes The device model as the hoot names it, such as TalonFX, Pigeon2 or CANcoder can_id yes Its CAN id, 0 to 62 subsystem yes The subsystem it belongs to, such as drivetrain or intake. Filters and History group by it role yes What it does, in words: front-left drive gear_ratio no Motor turns per mechanism turn, for mechanism-speed readouts swaps no Dates (2026-03-02, unquoted) the device in this slot was replaced. For logs with no CAN inventory only, each date starts a new history (a new legacy unit). With an inventory, Flashpoint follows serial numbers and ignores them

items.title: [[bus]]: the robot code's bus names
items.text:
Key What it does name The bus name your robot code uses, such as DriveTrain hoot The hoot bus it is: rio, canivore, or a CANivore's hex id

CAN bus status and Live CAN name buses the way robot code does. This table ties those names to the hoot's. Bus names must be unique.

items.title: [[signal]]: a value from the log
items.text:
A signal brings a NetworkTables value (subsystem state, PhotonVision) or a wpilog entry into Flashpoint.

Key What it does id A short name, unique in the file root A root from the season file, such as robot, photonvision or flashpoint entry The rest of the entry name after the root subsystem The subsystem it belongs to component Optional: the part of the subsystem, such as a bus name for CAN bus status metric What it measures, in snake_case, such as at_setpoint

Numbers are stored as numbers, and true/false as 1/0. A declared entry that a log doesn't have, or that isn't a number, is listed as a warning when derive runs. No two signals may map the same root and entry. CAN bus status shows the five signals per bus that CAN health needs.

items.title: [[siblings]]: slots compared with each other
items.text:
Key What it does name The group's name, unique in the file slots Two or more slot ids. A slot can be in only one group

The SIBLING anomaly method compares each slot with the median of its group, so put motors that do the same job together: the four drive motors, or a shooter's two flywheels. With no groups, there are no SIBLING findings.

items.title: The battery proxy
items.text: battery_proxy names a low-current device on the main power bus, such as the gyro, whose supply voltage stands in for the battery: Replay's battery track, brownout markers and brownout findings use it. A motor is a bad choice, because its own wiring drop under load reads as a brownout. With no proxy, Flashpoint uses the median supply voltage across devices, and a brownout found that way is at most MED. See Battery voltage and the PDH.

items.title: Adding both to a drafted file
items.text:
A drafted robot file (from Draft robot, or your first import) has neither a battery proxy nor sibling groups, because a log can't tell Flashpoint which devices do the same job. Add them by hand: battery_proxy at the top level, and one [[siblings]] block per group, using the slot ids the draft wrote (the model and CAN id, such as talonfx-11). You can rename the slots first; use whatever ids the file has.

robot = "2026-comp"
season = 2026
project = "Robot-2026"
battery_proxy = "pigeon2-10"   # added: the drafted gyro slot

# ... the drafted [[slot]] blocks stay as they are ...

[[siblings]]                   # added: the four drive motors
name = "drive"
slots = ["talonfx-11", "talonfx-21", "talonfx-31", "talonfx-41"]

[[siblings]]                   # added: the shooter's two flywheels
name = "flywheel"
slots = ["talonfx-5", "talonfx-6"]

Then run flashpoint derive --all. The Anomalies view says why both make findings more trustworthy.

items.title: Which robot file a log uses
items.text:
A log's season is the calendar year it was recorded in. Flashpoint takes the robot files for that season. If there's only one, that's the one. If there are several (a practice bot and a comp bot), it picks the one whose project matches the project name the robot code wrote into the log. With no match, the log's matches show robot "unknown" and their motors stay unmapped. Logs from December testing of next season's robot count as this season, so give that robot a file for this season too, or wait until January.

After editing a robot file, run flashpoint derive --all. You don't need to re-ingest.

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
flashpoint doctor checks every robot file and names the file and key:

  • A key the file doesn't take (here gearing for gear_ratio, in the first slot): 
    robots/2026-comp.toml: slot.0.gearing: Extra inputs are not permitted
  • A bus that isn't rio, canivore or a hex id (bus names are lower case): 
    robots/2026-comp.toml: slot.0.bus: bus must be 'rio', 'canivore', or a 32-hex CANivore id
  • A battery proxy that isn't a slot id: 
    robots/2026-comp.toml: battery proxy 'pigeon' is not one of the slots
  • A signal whose root the season file doesn't define (add the root to seasons/2026.toml): 
    robots/2026-comp.toml: 2026-comp.toml: signal 'a' names root 'robot', which season 2026 does not define

items.title: Season files (seasons/*.toml)
items.text:
A season file names the entry prefixes (roots) that a season's logs use, so a robot file's [[signal]] tables can say root = "robot" instead of the whole name. Flashpoint ships one per season (2026) with the roots every WPILib robot shares. To add your robot code's own root, copy it to seasons/2026.toml in your config folder and set robot. Ignite's is config/seasons/2026.toml:

season = 2026

[roots]
robot = "NT:Robot/m_robotContainer/"
photonvision = "NT:/photonvision/"
camera_publisher = "NT:/CameraPublisher/"
preferences = "NT:/Preferences/"
fms = "NT:/FMSInfo/"
flashpoint = "/Flashpoint/"

Your file replaces the bundled one whole, so keep every root in it.

Key Required What it is season yes The year. It must match the file name roots yes The [roots] table robot no In [roots]: your robot code's NetworkTables root. Until it's set, robot-code signals are reported as missing photonvision yes In [roots]: PhotonVision's NetworkTables root camera_publisher yes In [roots]: the camera server's root preferences yes In [roots]: WPILib Preferences fms yes In [roots]: the FMS info the Driver Station publishes, which gives the match flashpoint no In [roots]: where robot code writes Flashpoint's own wpilog entries (/Flashpoint/): the CAN inventory and bus status

NetworkTables entries appear in the wpilog as NT: followed by the topic, which is why most roots start that way. Start a new season covers making next year's file.

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
From flashpoint doctor:

  • A file that leaves out bundled roots (here everything but robot): 
    seasons/2026.toml: roots.photonvision: Field required; roots.camera_publisher: Field required; roots.preferences: Field required; roots.fms: Field required
  • A robot file whose signal uses a root this file doesn't have: see robot file errors.

items.title: theme.toml
items.text:
theme.toml sets the team name and number in the app header, and the app's colours. With no file, Flashpoint uses the bundled default: amber, and the header reads "telemetry". Set the team name and colours does this through the Setup view.

team_name = "Robo Rams"    # optional, at most 40 characters
# team_number = 1234       # optional, display only; defaults to `team` in acquire.toml
palette = "custom"         # amber, green, blue, red, white, or "custom"

[custom]                   # only with palette = "custom"
primary = "#00A3E0"        # #RRGGBB
# background = "#0A0806"   # optional
# warning = "#FF5A1F"      # optional; picked for you when left out
Key Default What it does team_name none The name in the header, 1 to 40 characters team_number team from acquire.toml The number shown next to it. Display only palette amber A preset (amber, green, blue, red or white, all on a dark background) or custom custom none The [custom] table. Required with palette = "custom", refused with a preset primary (required) In [custom]: the main colour, #RRGGBB background the amber background In [custom]: the page background warning worked out from primary In [custom]: the warning colour

Flashpoint works out every other shade from those colours, and refuses a palette that's hard to read:

  • every text shade needs at least 4.5:1 contrast on every background shade;
  • boundary lines need at least 3:1 on the background;
  • the warning colour needs 4.5:1 too, and must stand apart from the primary: at least 35° apart in hue, or 25 % apart in lightness.

items.title: Common errors
items.text:
A broken theme.toml doesn't stop the app: it starts with the default amber and no name, and flashpoint doctor shows a PROBLEM on theme.toml with one of these:

  • A misspelt key: 
    theme.toml: pallete: Extra inputs are not permitted
  • An unknown palette: 
    theme.toml: palette 'purple' is not one of ['amber', 'green', 'blue', 'red', 'white', 'custom']
  • custom without a [custom] table: 
    theme.toml: palette = "custom" needs a [custom] table with primary
  • A colour that isn't #RRGGBB: 
    theme.toml: custom.primary: expected a #RRGGBB colour such as #00A3E0, not 'blue'
  • A name over 40 characters: 
    theme.toml: team_name: String should have at most 40 characters
  • A palette that fails the contrast rules. The message lists each failing pair and ends with a suggestion, for example: 
    theme.toml: palette refused: text contrast: accent #101010 on surface-raised #15100A is 1.01:1, needs at least 4.5:1; ... nearest primary that passes: #808080

items.title: The motor list (units/units-seed.csv)
items.text:
units/units-seed.csv lists every physical CTRE device the team owns, by factory serial number, with the label on it. Flashpoint uses it to start each motor's history, including spares on the shelf that never appear in a log. After that, the robot's CAN inventory keeps it current. It's optional: without it, motors still get histories, from the inventory or from slots.

flashpoint init writes the file with just its header. Ignite's README for it walks through filling it in from Tuner X.

serial,model,robot,bus,can_id,role,label,first_installed,notes
6E9415C3394C4853,Talon FX,2026-comp,DriveTrain,11,FL drive,M-014,2026-01-20,rebuilt gearbox 2026-03
Column Example Notes serial 6E9415C3394C4853 Exactly as Tuner X shows it model Talon FX Device model robot 2026-comp A robot name, or shelf for a spare bus rio or the CANivore name Blank for shelf can_id 11 Blank for shelf role FL drive The slot's role on the robot. Blank for shelf label M-014 The physical label on the motor. Never reuse one first_installed 2026-01-20 A best guess is fine notes rebuilt gearbox 2026-03 Free text

items.title: View: Anomalies
items.text: Status: beta (#77). Detection is tuned on one team's robots (ours), so a finding is a suggestion to check against its evidence, not a verdict. The Anomalies view is the queue of everything detection flagged: each anomaly with its evidence, a severity, likely causes to check, and what the team did about it (triage). It needs flashpoint serve; a static export doesn't have it. Make findings trustworthy says how to get better findings on your robot.

items.title: What beta means today
items.text:
Detection has been tuned on one team's robots, so treat every finding as something to check, not a fault you already know about. What the app does about that (#77):

  • The view's header shows a BETA tag and a one-line note that says this, with a link to this page. It's there whatever the counts, including when nothing is flagged.
  • A brownout found on the median fallback (no battery_proxy declared) is at most MED. Its why says the fallback can read wiring drops as brownouts, and that declaring a battery-proxy slot makes the finding trustworthy.
  • The spread floors for isolated CAN gaps and CAN frames missed per minute scale with a device's frame rate. A device at 125 frames per second or slower, which covers roboRIO-bus rates, keeps the configured floors. Above that, each floor is multiplied by the rate ÷ 50, so a 250 Hz CANivore device gets five times the floor. Normal timing jitter on a CANivore then stays inside the band, and a real dropout still stands out. The SPEC limit on the longest gap doesn't scale. The why of a CAN-gap DRIFT, STEP or SIBLING finding states the device's frame rate and the floor it was judged with. To make CAN-gap findings rarer, raise floors in anomaly.toml.
  • Temperature that isn't logged never raises a finding. On hoots without Phoenix Pro, detection skips temperature and judges current and CAN as usual; see Phoenix Pro and temperature.

items.title: Make findings trustworthy
items.text:
Three things in your configuration make findings more trustworthy:

  1. Declare a battery proxy slot. Brownouts are judged on the robot file's battery_proxy: a low-current device on the main power bus, such as the gyro. With none, Flashpoint uses the median supply voltage across devices, which can read wiring drops under load as brownouts. The anomaly's "Why it was flagged" text names the proxy it used, such as "median of 12 devices".
  2. Declare sibling groups. SIBLING compares each motor with the others in its [[siblings]] group: the four drive motors, or a shooter's two flywheels. With no groups, there are no SIBLING findings, and a motor that drifts along with its neighbours (a shared cause, such as a hot day) isn't told apart from one that leaves them.
  3. Let units build their baseline. DRIFT and STEP judge a unit against its own earlier matches, and need min_baseline of them first (5 by default, anomaly.toml). Until then the unit is "building baseline". Confidence stays Low until the baseline holds 10 matches. After a deliberate change, such as a new gearbox, dismiss the anomaly and restart the unit's baseline (below), so the old normal doesn't keep flagging the new one.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Part What it holds Filter bar SEASON, ROBOT, EVENT and the UNIT chip (the header and filter bar) Summary band The open count, SHOW and SENSITIVITY QUEUE rail (left) GROUP, the queue, and HOW FLASHPOINT FLAGS THINGS Main column The selected anomaly's detail

The ◂ button at the top of the rail shrinks it to a strip labelled QUEUE; press the strip to bring it back. Your browser remembers this for Anomalies.

items.title: Summary band
items.text:
• The large number is the open anomalies that pass the filters at the chosen sensitivity. It's highlighted when any of them is HIGH. Under it: "n high ·" and "scanned through match key", the latest match detection judged, or "nothing scanned yet".
  • SHOW picks the queue: OPEN, RESOLVED or DISMISSED, each with its count, such as OPEN · 3. Open means NEW or INVESTIGATING.
  • SENSITIVITY: RELAXED, NORMAL or STRICT (below).

The count on the ANOMALIES tab is different: it is always the open anomalies at normal sensitivity, across the whole lake, whatever the filters.

items.title: Methods
items.text:
HOW FLASHPOINT FLAGS THINGS, under the queue, lists the methods:

Method Fires when Settings SPEC A fixed limit (temperature, stall, reboots, CAN gaps, brownouts) was crossed in a match [spec] STEP A unit jumped away from its own history and stayed there [baseline] DRIFT A unit moved slowly away from its own history [baseline] SIBLING A unit left the others that do the same job, in the same matches [sibling] MODEL An optional model found an unusual mix of features (off by default) [model]

items.title: Severity
items.text: Method HIGH, MED, LOW SPEC The highest level any match of the anomaly reached, from the [spec] limits. A reboot while enabled is HIGH; while disabled, MED STEP, DRIFT, SIBLING How far outside the baseline, in spreads (z): HIGH at high_z or more, MED at med_z or more, LOW below MODEL As for STEP, but never above MED

items.title: Sensitivity
items.text:
Sensitivity changes what is shown, never what is computed:

Setting Shows RELAXED MED and HIGH only NORMAL Every severity (the default) STRICT Also the anomalies that only the lower [strict] thresholds find (anomaly.toml)

SPEC anomalies show at every sensitivity, and MODEL anomalies at normal and strict only. Your browser remembers the setting, and Replay's anomaly marks use it too. It's also in the address, so a copied link keeps it.

items.title: Queue
items.text:
The heading reads TAB · n · HIGHEST SEVERITY FIRST. Anomalies are sorted by severity, then by their most recent flagged match. HIGH ones are highlighted. Each one shows:

  • its severity and subject: the slot's role (or slot id), or "Battery · robot" for a robot's brownouts;
  • its method;
  • its title, such as "Supply path resistance stepped up from 18 mΩ to 31 mΩ at Q12";
  • an EVENT BOUNDARY · GADAL → GACMP badge when a STEP started with the unit's first match at a new event;
  • "since match", the match it started in;
  • its state: NEW, INVESTIGATING, RESOLVED or DISMISSED, with " · NO LONGER DETECTED" when the latest detection run doesn't produce it any more (below).

Select one to see its detail.

GROUP sets how the queue is laid out. NONE is a plain list. DEVICE groups it by physical unit, named "role · SN serial" (or "legacy id"), with a robot's brownouts under "Battery · robot". Each group shows its count and worst severity, and the groups are ordered the same way as the anomalies. Press a group's heading (▾ or ▸) to fold it. Folding isn't remembered; the grouping is, in the address.

items.title: Header
items.text:
• The severity, method and state.
  • The subject, then its model, "SN serial" (or "legacy id" or "battery proxy"), slot and robot.
  • unit history, which opens History with this unit selected and the closest metric, or open in Replay (battery track) for a brownout.
  • The triage buttons (below).

items.title: Facts
items.text:
The title, then:

Fact What it is ACTUAL The value: the worst value for SPEC, the median of the flagged matches otherwise EXPECTED The limit for SPEC (such as "< 65 °C"), the baseline and its spread for STEP and DRIFT, or "within x of group" for SIBLING FIRST SEEN The match it started in MATCHES AFFECTED Flagged matches. A run of flagged matches with up to two unflagged ones between them is one anomaly CONFIDENCE Low, Medium or High. Low when the baseline has fewer than 10 matches or only one match is flagged; High when it has 20 or more and at least 3 matches are flagged METHOD SPEC, STEP, DRIFT, SIBLING or MODEL

Badges under the facts:

  • ▲ LOW ALIGNMENT IN A FLAGGED MATCH: at least one flagged match's hoot and wpilog clocks couldn't be matched with high confidence. Check it in Replay.
  • EVENT BOUNDARY · GADAL → GACMP · STARTED AT THE FIRST MATCH OF THE NEW EVENT: the STEP began when the unit moved to a new event. Check whether the mechanism or its configuration changed between events.

items.title: EVIDENCE
items.text:
A chart of the metric over the unit's matches, up to 40, ending at the latest flagged one:

Mark Meaning ━ (bright line) This unit's value per match ┅ (dashed line) The sibling group's median, for SIBLING ▒ (shaded band) The expected range ■ (large dot) A flagged match

The line above it names the competitions, and a dashed vertical line marks the start of each later one, as in History. Select a point to open that match in Replay, with this slot's tracks (or the battery track for a brownout).

items.title: WHY IT WAS FLAGGED and LIKELY CAUSES
items.text: WHY IT WAS FLAGGED says in a sentence what was compared and how far it moved. LIKELY CAUSES lists the causes to check for this method, metric and subsystem, from the team's catalogue (anomaly-causes.toml). It says "No causes recorded for this pattern yet" when the catalogue has none, or "The cause catalogue has an error:" and the error. Causes are suggestions, not a diagnosis.

items.title: SEEN THIS BEFORE, OUTCOME and HISTORY
items.text:
• SEEN THIS BEFORE lists resolved and dismissed anomalies with the same method and metric on this unit or this slot, each with what the team wrote. Otherwise: "No closed anomaly like this on this slot or unit yet."
  • OUTCOME, for a resolved or dismissed anomaly, is what the team wrote.
  • HISTORY lists every triage change, with its time, the states, "baseline restarted" when it applied, and the outcome.

items.title: Triage
items.text:
Triage records what the team did about an anomaly. The buttons depend on its state:

State Buttons NEW INVESTIGATE, DISMISS AS EXPECTED INVESTIGATING MARK RESOLVED, DISMISS AS EXPECTED RESOLVED REOPEN DISMISSED REOPEN
  • INVESTIGATE: someone is looking into it. It saves at once.
  • MARK RESOLVED: fixed. Write what was found or fixed in WHAT WAS FOUND OR FIXED.
  • DISMISS AS EXPECTED: not a problem. Write why in WHY THIS IS EXPECTED. Tick "Restart this unit's baseline for metric from the onset match (for example after a gearbox change)" so the unit's baseline for this metric starts again from the match the anomaly started in.
  • REOPEN: back to NEW.

The text is required, up to 500 characters, and is shown with the anomaly and in SEEN THIS BEFORE. Press SAVE · action to save it or CANCEL to close the form. A refused save shows "Not saved:" and the reason, such as "an outcome is required: say what was found or done".

A baseline restart starts flashpoint detect in the background. Until it has run, the detail says "Baseline restart pending: detection has not run since the restart was recorded. The queue updates when it does."

Triage is saved in the lake, never in the logs. When a later detection run no longer produces a triaged anomaly (its configuration or data changed), it stays in its tab with the title "No longer detected: metric from match" and the note "No longer detected: the latest detection run does not produce this anomaly (its configuration or data changed). Its triage is kept." See Triage an anomaly.

items.title: Filters
items.text:
The shared filters apply here on the server. An anomaly passes the season, robot and event filters when at least one of its flagged matches is in them. The unit filter keeps that unit's anomalies, which is how History's anomaly badges open this view.

  • When the selected anomaly doesn't pass the filters, it stays open and the queue says "The selected anomaly is hidden by the filters."
  • When nothing passes: "Nothing passes these filters.", which value no match in the lake has, and CLEAR FILTERS.

items.title: Empty and error states
items.text:
State What Anomalies shows Nothing open "Nothing is flagged at sensitivity sensitivity." (on another tab: "Nothing here.") Units without enough history "n unit(s) are still building their baseline (5 matches before DRIFT and STEP can judge them)." Detection never ran "Detection has not run on this lake yet: run flashpoint detect." Nothing selected "Pick an anomaly from the queue to see the evidence." The server can't answer Anomalies unavailable and the error

The baseline note always says 5 matches, even when min_baseline is set to something else.

items.title: Shared on the network
items.text: Triage is the app's one write to the lake, so it only works when serve is bound to this machine (the default). Started with flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0, the triage buttons are replaced by "Read-only: triage is only available on the machine running Flashpoint.", for everyone, the laptop included. Everything else works. Sensitivity and grouping are each viewer's own. See flashpoint serve.

items.title: View: History
items.text: History shows how each motor trends across every match in the lake: one point per match for a metric such as peak temperature, supply current or CAN gaps, with a line per physical motor (a unit, followed by serial number) or per position on the robot (a slot). Use it to spot a motor that runs hotter or draws more than it used to, to see where a unit has been, and to jump to the matches that stand out. It needs flashpoint serve; a static export doesn't have it.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Part What it holds Filter bar The shared filters, then History's own after HISTORY ONLY Summary tiles UNITS TRACKED, MATCHES, POWERED-ON H, UNITS WARN/HOT Main column The metric buttons, PER UNIT / PER SLOT, the chart, and the units table UNIT rail (right) The selected unit's totals, lifeline and matches

The ▸ button at the top of the rail shrinks it to a strip labelled UNIT; press the strip to bring it back. Your browser remembers this for History.

History lists motors: devices that log stator current. Usage totals (POWERED-ON H and the rail's totals) also count sessions that aren't competition matches, such as shop and practice-field logs.

items.title: Filters
items.text:
SEASON, ROBOT, EVENT and the UNIT chip are the filters every view shares (the header and filter bar). Selecting a unit in the table or on the chart sets the unit filter, so it follows you to Replay and Anomalies.

After HISTORY ONLY come four filters that affect History only. History keeps them when you leave and come back through its tab.

Filter Choices TYPE All types, Qualification, Practice, Elimination, Semifinal, Final (the types the lake has) PHASE MATCH (the whole match, the default), AUTO, TELEOP SUBSYSTEM All subsystems, or one from the robot files SLOT All slots, or one slot id

CLEAR FILTERS clears History's own filters too. Every filter runs as a query on the laptop running serve; nothing is filtered in the browser.

items.title: Summary tiles
items.text:
The tiles cover the filtered range:

Tile What it counts UNITS TRACKED Units with at least one match MATCHES Matches POWERED-ON H Hours the units were powered, over every session in range (the phase filter doesn't apply) UNITS WARN/HOT Units whose health (below) is WARN or HOT

items.title: Metric and lines
items.text:
The metric buttons pick what the chart and table show:

Button Per match Unit PEAK TEMPERATURE The highest temperature °C LOWEST SUPPLY VOLTAGE The lowest supply voltage V SUPPLY ENERGY Energy drawn from the battery Wh STALL TIME Time stalled s SUPPLY CURRENT P95 The 95th percentile of supply current A REBOOTS Device reboots count ISOLATED CAN GAPS CAN frame gaps on this device alone count CAN FRAMES MISSED PER ENABLED MINUTE Missed CAN frames /min LONGEST ISOLATED CAN GAP The longest gap on this device alone ms

The CAN metrics come from the CAN frames in the hoots.

PER UNIT draws one line per unit, following its serial number across slots and robots. PER SLOT draws one line per slot, named robot/slot, whichever unit was in it. A motor swapped into a slot shows as a new line per unit and the same line per slot.

The heading names the metric, its unit, and the reference value when there is one.

items.title: Chart
items.text:
• One point per match, in time order. The axis labels are the match part of the key (qm7).
  • The line above the chart names the competitions: "COMPETITION · GACMP", or "COMPETITIONS · GADAL · 12 MATCHES → GACMP · 15 MATCHES" when there's more than one. A year is added to the names when the range spans more than one season.
  • A dashed vertical line marks the start of each later competition, labelled with its event. A label that would overlap the one before it is left off; the line above the chart still names every competition.
  • A dashed horizontal REF line shows the reference value: temp_warn_c for peak temperature and voltage_danger_v for lowest supply voltage (report.toml). The other metrics have none.
  • A match is shaded when its alignment confidence isn't high.
  • With a unit selected (per unit), its line is drawn bright and thicker, with a warning-coloured dot on its low-alignment matches and a larger dot (◆ in the legend) where it changed slot.
  • A gap in a line is a match the unit wasn't installed for.

Point at the chart to see the match key and time. When the pointer is near a line, that line lights up and the readout adds the unit or slot, its value, its slot, the alignment, and "slot changed" when it moved. With no line near, the readout uses the selected unit's point.

Pressing the chart:

Press on Per unit Per slot Another unit's line Selects that unit The selected unit's point, or near no other line Opens that match in Replay, with that slot's tracks A slot's line Opens that match in Replay, with that slot's tracks Anywhere else Updates the readout only Updates the readout only

The legend under the chart names the selected unit ("select a unit to emphasise it" when there's none), the other lines, the reference, the low-alignment shading and the slot-change mark, when each is on the chart.

items.title: Units table
items.text:
The heading reads UNITS · n IN RANGE · metric. There's one row per unit in range:

Column What it shows UNIT · SLOT The slot's role (or slot id), then the slot. Press it to select the unit; press it again to clear the selection SERIAL The serial number, or the unit id for a legacy unit IN SERVICE First and last day it was seen in range MATCHES Matches in range LATEST The metric in its latest match CHANGE Latest minus first, with a sign TREND A sparkline of the metric per match. Every row shares one scale, from zero unless a value is negative; hover for the unit's range and the shared scale HEALTH A status word, and an anomaly badge when it has open anomalies

items.title: Health
items.text:
Status When OK The unit's highest temperature in range is below temp_warn_c WARN At or above temp_warn_c HOT At or above temp_fault_c NO DATA No temperature in range

Open anomalies at normal sensitivity raise it: a HIGH anomaly makes the unit HOT, a MED or LOW one makes it at least WARN. The badge beside it, such as 2 HIGH, is the count and worst severity of those anomalies, and opens them in Anomalies.

Health reads temperature only, so a motor with no temperature, such as one on a hoot without Phoenix Pro, shows NO DATA (Phoenix Pro and temperature). The limits are in report.toml.

items.title: UNIT rail
items.text:
With no unit selected: "Select a unit in the table to see its odometry and lifeline."

For a selected unit:

  • its model and serial ("SN serial", or "legacy id"), its current role or slot, and its health. Here health is from temperature alone, over every match, so it can differ from the table's;
  • totals, filtered by season and robot only: MATCHES IN SERVICE, POWERED-ON (h), SUPPLY ENERGY (Wh), THERMAL CYCLES, STALL (s), MAX TEMPERATURE (°C);
  • "Sessions without aligned samples: n (not counted above)";
  • LIFELINE, newest first: First seen, Moved, Replaced by unit, Last seen, each with the date, the match key (or "practice"), the robot and slot, the bus and CAN id, and whether it came from a CAN inventory or a legacy epoch (CAN inventory);
  • MATCHES: its 12 most recent matches in range, each with REPLAY match key, which opens it in Replay with that slot's tracks, and LOGS, which lists that match's raw logs below with download links and OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE. If the match has no Replay data yet, it says "Replay data for this match is not built: run flashpoint report --match <key>";
  • LINK TO THIS UNIT, an address that opens History with this unit selected.

A unit id that isn't in the lake (from an old link) shows "Not found", "No unit id in this lake." and the CLOSEST ids, as links.

items.title: Empty and error states
items.text: State What History shows No match features in the lake No matches ingested: "The lake at lake has no match features yet." and "Ingest logs with flashpoint ingest <folder of .wpilog and .hoot files>, then reload." The filters leave no match "No matches in this range.", and which filter value no match in the lake has The server can't answer History unavailable and the error

items.title: Shared on the network
items.text: History changes nothing, so it works the same from another computer (flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0), except that the OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE under LOGS says "Open in AdvantageScope is only available on the machine running Flashpoint. Use the downloads below." With --host 0.0.0.0 that is true on the laptop itself too. Selecting a unit only changes your own page address. See flashpoint serve.

items.title: View: Live CAN
items.text:
Status: experimental. Live CAN needs robot code that publishes CAN health (Adding it to robot code), and it can report false dropouts on fast buses: on our robot's CANivore, with signals at 250 Hz, gaps under 15 ms were counted as dropouts. Until a per-bus dropout window (#66) lands and the pit check on a real robot passes, treat a lone dropout on a fast bus with suspicion and confirm it after the match in Replay's CAN markers. The Live CAN view reads the robot while you work on it, and shows which CTRE device dropped out, rebooted or faulted, and whether it was one device or the whole bus. Use it for a shake test (robot disabled, wiggle each harness) or a drive test (robot enabled). It records nothing: the lake and the configuration don't change.

How to set up the robot code and run a test is in Live CAN health. This page describes what's on the screen.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Part What it holds Band LIVE CAN, the connection pill, the enabled pill, the robot line, and MARK Message What's wrong with the connection, when something is Bus panels One per CAN bus: its counts, then a card per device EVENTS The event log, newest first

There are no filters on this view. It needs flashpoint serve; a static export doesn't have it.

items.title: Connection pill
items.text:
Pill Meaning CONNECTING Looking for the robot. The message says "Looking for the robot. Turn it on and join its network; this keeps trying." WAITING FOR DATA Connected less than a second ago, and robot code hasn't published its version yet CONNECTED Connected, and robot code publishes live CAN health this Flashpoint can read NOT PUBLISHING Connected, but robot code doesn't publish live CAN health UNSUPPORTED VERSION Robot code publishes a contract version this Flashpoint doesn't support

Flashpoint connects to the robot from the laptop running serve, at the addresses flashpoint acquire uses (from your team number, or hosts in acquire.toml), or the ones given with flashpoint serve --robot-host (flashpoint serve). It connects only while a Live CAN view is open somewhere, and disconnects about 30 seconds after the last one closes.

items.title: Enabled pill and robot line
items.text:
• ENABLED or DISABLED, as robot code reports it, or a dash before it has.
  • The robot line: "robot address" once connected ("trying addresses" before), "project name" from robot code, and "config robot", the robot file whose project matches.

items.title: MARK
items.text: Type what you're about to do in MARK ("now wiggling: FL module"), at most 60 characters, and press Enter or SET. Every event after that carries the mark, until you set another or press CLEAR. Beside it: "marking: mark", or "no mark".

items.title: Bus panels
items.text:
Each bus has a heading with its name (as robot code names it, such as rio or DriveTrain), then:

  • BUS DROPPED, for 5 seconds after a bus-wide dropout;
  • "n reporting", and "· m missing" when devices in the robot file aren't reported;
  • UTILISATION, the share of the bus in use;
  • BUS OFF, TX FULL, RX ERRORS and TX ERRORS, robot code's counts for the bus;
  • BUS-WIDE DROPS, how many bus-wide dropouts the bus has had since Flashpoint connected.

items.title: Device cards
items.text:
A card per device, slots first (by slot id), then unmapped devices. Each shows its slot (or "unmapped"), its state, the slot's role, the device name (such as TalonFX-11), its dropout and reset totals since Flashpoint connected ("n drops", "n resets"), its lowest supply voltage in the latest update, and any fault names (under-voltage, boot during enable, hardware, bridge brownout, bad magnet).

A card shows one state, the first that applies:

State Meaning DISCONNECTED Robot code says it isn't heard at all DROPPED Had an isolated dropout in the last 5 seconds REBOOTED Reset in the last 5 seconds FAULTED A fault bit is set in its latest update OK Heard, nothing new UNMAPPED Reported, but no slot in the robot file matches its bus, model and CAN id MISSING In the robot file, but robot code doesn't report it: check it's wired, powered, and registered in robot code. Its card says "configured, not reported"

DISCONNECTED, DROPPED and REBOOTED use the FAULT colour, FAULTED the WARN colour, and MISSING and UNMAPPED the NO DATA grey.

items.title: Isolated or bus-wide
items.text: A dropout is bus-wide when at least half of the bus's other reporting devices also dropped in the same update. It's one BUS DROP event, counted in BUS-WIDE DROPS and not against any device. Otherwise it's isolated: a DROPOUT event, charged to that device. Updates arrive about every 100 ms, so a dropout that spans two updates can show as two isolated dropouts.

items.title: EVENTS
items.text:
One line per event, newest first, up to 500. Each line has the time (to the millisecond), ENABLED or DISABLED, what happened, the mark if one was set, and the device or bus:

Event What it shows DROPOUT slot (device) on bus, "×n" dropouts, and the oldest signal age in ms BUS DROP bus: every device that dropped, how many, and the oldest age REBOOT slot (device) on bus, "×n" resets FAULT slot (device) on bus, and the fault's name LOST slot (device) on bus, "not heard" BACK slot (device) on bus, "heard again" BUS ERR bus, and which counts rose, such as "+2 rx errors" RESTART "robot code restarted", "totals start again"

Robot code counts from when it started. When its totals go down, Flashpoint takes it as a robot code restart: one RESTART event, and counting starts again without reporting the drop as dropouts or reboots.

Before the first event: "No events yet. They appear here as the robot reports them."

items.title: Messages
items.text: Message When "No robot address. Run flashpoint init --team <number>, or start the server with flashpoint serve --robot-host <address>." There's no team number and no address to try "Looking for the robot. Turn it on and join its network; this keeps trying." Not connected yet "The robot is connected, but its code is not publishing live CAN health under /Flashpoint/Live/CANHealth/. To add it to robot code, see the Live CAN health guide, "Adding it to robot code"." NOT PUBLISHING "The robot publishes live CAN health version n; this Flashpoint supports version m. Update Flashpoint or the robot code so they match." UNSUPPORTED VERSION. Nothing else shows "No robot configuration has project name, so every device shows unmapped. Add or fix a robot file in Setup." No robot file has the project robot code publishes (robot files) "Ignored:" and the topics, each with why (such as "wrong type: string" or "negative count: -1") Robot code publishes a topic with a bad value. The rest keeps working

items.title: Shared on the network
items.text: Live CAN changes nothing, so it works the same from another computer (flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0). The laptop running serve holds the one connection to the robot. Device totals come from it, so everyone watching sees the same totals, and they survive a reload. Marks and the event log stay in each browser: reloading the page clears them, and other people watching don't see yours.

items.title: View: Replay
items.text: Replay shows one competition match on a shared timeline: battery voltage, current and temperature tracks, rule markers for what went wrong and when, and a readout of every motor. Use it after a match to see what happened, and to hand the raw logs to AdvantageScope for a frame-by-frame look. It works in flashpoint serve and in a static export on a USB stick (Take Replay on a USB stick).

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Part What it holds Filter bar SEASON, ROBOT and EVENT, which narrow the match list (below) MATCHES rail (left) The match list, grouped by event Main column The match header, notes, the timeline (markers, four tracks, scrub bar) and COMPARE DETAILS rail (right) The selected marker, the readout, and OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE with the raw log downloads

On a wide screen each rail scrolls on its own. The ◂ and ▸ buttons at the top of a rail shrink it to a strip labelled MATCHES or DETAILS; press the strip to bring it back. Your browser remembers this for Replay, per side.

Replay lists only competition matches: a log is a match when the wpilog has FMS data or a match-style file name (How matches are identified). Practice and pit logs count in History, not here.

items.title: The header and filter bar
items.text:
These are the same on every view.

  • The tabs REPLAY, HISTORY, ANOMALIES, SETUP and LIVE CAN. A static export has only REPLAY.
  • The ANOMALIES tab carries a count of open anomalies at normal sensitivity, across the whole lake, whatever the filters. It is highlighted when any of them is HIGH.
  • The SETUP tab carries a ! badge while the lake's backup is overdue (overdue_h in acquire.toml).
  • On the right: the lake folder (served), or a STATIC EXPORT pill, and CRT, which turns the scanline texture on and off. This browser remembers the CRT setting.

The filter bar sits under the header on Replay, History and Anomalies:

  • SEASON, ROBOT and EVENT pickers, newest first. Choosing a season narrows the robot and event lists to it.
  • A UNIT chip when a unit is selected (from History). Press its ✕ to remove it.
  • CLEAR FILTERS clears every filter. It is greyed out when nothing is set.

A filter set in one view stays set in the others, and it's in the address, so a copied link keeps it. A value no match has (from an old link) stays chosen and is marked "(not in this index)" here, or "(not in this lake)" in History and Anomalies.

items.title: Match list
items.text:
Each match is a button showing:

  • its label (Q7, E10, P3, SF2, F1) and the robot and start time;
  • the worst severity (HIGH, MED or LOW) of the open anomalies flagged in it, at the sensitivity last chosen in the Anomalies view. Hover over it for the count;
  • its markers: n FAULT and n WARN, or 0 MARKERS when no rule fired;
  • NO ALIGNED SAMPLES instead of marker counts when the match has no data to chart (below);
  • ▲ LOW ALIGNMENT · alignment when the hoot and wpilog clocks couldn't be matched with high confidence.

Events are listed in reverse order of their event key (2026gacmp, 2026gadal), so a later season comes first; matches within an event are in start order. Selecting a match opens it.

items.title: Filters in Replay
items.text:
• With no filter in the address at all (a fresh link), Replay picks the selected match's season and event, or the latest match's.
  • The unit filter isn't applied, because the match list doesn't record which units played each match. The chip says "not applied in Replay".
  • If the match data was built by an older Flashpoint, SEASON is greyed out with "Rebuild with flashpoint report to filter by season."
  • When the filters leave no match: "No matches for these filters.", which value no match has, and a CLEAR FILTERS button.
  • When the open match isn't in the filtered list: "Selected match label is hidden by the filters."

items.title: Match header
items.text:
• The match label and key, and COPY LINK, which copies the page address (it reads COPIED for a moment). The address holds the match, the tracks, the cursor, the selected marker, the zoom window, the overlay and the filters.
  • A line of facts: robot, event, start, duration, alignment (with the method), and the log files.
  • Notes, when they apply:
Note Shown when "▲ Low alignment confidence (alignment): hoot and wpilog times may disagree. Check events against AdvantageScope." Alignment isn't high "Temperature not logged." followed by "The hoots are not Pro-licensed, so they carry no temperature." or "No temperature was logged for this match." No slot has temperature (Phoenix Pro and temperature) "No match phases were found (the robot was never enabled in this log), so time is measured from the first sample and the whole log is shown." The log has no auto, teleop or test phase "n more session(s) share this match key (m without aligned samples); their raw logs are listed below." Several sessions have the same match key "n slot(s) log current slower than 20 Hz (slots); spikes between their samples are not visible." A slot's current logs slower than 20 Hz (Signal rates)

items.title: Window and zoom
items.text:
The WINDOW line shows the visible span, such as "T+12.0 – T+48.5 s". Every track and the marker strip share it.

Control What it does − Zoom out by a factor of two + Zoom in by a factor of two FULL MATCH Show the whole match Shift-drag on a track Zoom to the dragged span Ctrl or ⌘ + scroll, or a trackpad pinch Zoom around the pointer + or = Zoom in, while a timeline control (a marker or a zoom button) has focus - or _ Zoom out 0 Full match

The narrowest window is half a second. Zooming centres on the cursor when it's in view.

Replay stores each match in up to 1,000 time buckets (fewer for a long match, to keep each match's file small). Zoomed in to less than half the match, the served app fetches finer data from the lake for the visible window, and the line reads "n ms buckets from the lake". Until it arrives, or in a static export, it reads "bucket resolution (n ms)". If finer data can't be had, it adds "finer data unavailable:" and the reason, such as "Rebuild with flashpoint report to zoom past bucket resolution."

items.title: Markers
items.text:
Markers sit in a strip above the tracks: ▲ for WARN, ✕ for FAULT. Hover over one for its message. Selecting one moves the window to it if needed, puts the cursor on it, and shows it in the MARKER panel on the right. Markers outside the window are hidden and counted at the edges, as ◂ n and n ▸; press a count to select the nearest hidden marker on that side.

Markers come from fixed rules and state what the log shows. They don't name a cause. The thresholds are in report.toml:

Marker Level Source Fires when Message Temperature WARN the slot Temperature rises to temp_warn_c "Temperature n °C" Temperature FAULT the slot Temperature rises to temp_fault_c "Temperature n °C" Brownout FAULT power The battery proxy stays below brownout_v for at least brownout_hold_s "Battery proxy (proxy) v V (below limit V) for t s" Sag WARN power The battery proxy goes below sag_v, outside a brownout Same form as brownout Stall WARN the slot Stator current is at least 20 % of the motor's stall current while the rotor turns slower than 0.5 rps "Stalled t s, stator up to n A" Reboot FAULT the slot The device reset during the match "Device rebooted", with the reset count before and after when the log has it Dropout WARN the slot One device's CAN frames stopped for at least dropout_warn_s while others still talked "No CAN frames for t s" Bus gap WARN bus:name A whole CAN bus was silent for at least sample_gap_s "Whole bus silent for t s"

A temperature marker fires each time the temperature crosses a limit going up. Low-voltage dips less than a second apart are one marker. The battery proxy is the robot file's battery_proxy slot, or the median supply voltage across devices when there is none. The stall rule's 20 % and 0.5 rps are fixed in Flashpoint, not in report.toml. CAN markers need the hoots' CAN data. They name the bus by the robot code's name when the robot file has a [[bus]] entry for it.

items.title: Tracks
items.text:
There are four tracks. By default they are:

  1. Battery proxy (V), labelled with the proxy it uses: a slot, "median of n devices", or "not logged". A dashed reference line marks BROWNOUT at brownout_v.
  2. Total supply current (A), the sum of every slot's supply current.
  3. The temperature of the hottest motor, with a dashed WARN line at temp_warn_c.
  4. The supply current of the highest-current motor.

Opened from History or Anomalies for one slot, track 4 shows that slot's supply current, and track 3 its temperature when it logged one.

Each track's label shows its name, the value at the cursor, and its lowest and highest value in the window ("no samples" when there are none). The picker under it swaps the track for Battery proxy (V), Total supply current (A), or any slot's supply current, stator current, rotor velocity, motor voltage or temperature. A track a slot didn't log reads "not logged", which isn't the same as zero.

The battery and per-slot current, velocity and voltage lines are the mean per bucket, with a shaded band between the bucket's minimum and maximum. Temperature is drawn as it changed, with no band. Auto and teleop are shaded behind the lines, auto a little darker. A value carries forward for up to a second over empty buckets, so slow signals draw as lines.

Under a track's picker, a badge appears for each open anomaly flagged in this match on that slot (the battery track shows the robot's battery anomalies): its method and title, such as "STEP · Supply current P95 stepped up ...". It opens the anomaly in the Anomalies view. In a static export the badge can't open anything and says when its snapshot was taken.

items.title: Cursor
items.text: Press or drag on any track to place the cursor; the SCRUB slider does the same. The time shows beside it ("no cursor" when there's none). MAXIMA removes the cursor, and the readout goes back to each motor's match maximum.

items.title: COMPARE
items.text: COMPARE overlays another match with aligned samples, drawn dashed on every track and aligned on match time. Pick "no overlay" to remove it. The readout gains two columns for the overlay match; a slot that match didn't have reads "absent".

items.title: MARKER
items.text: The selected marker's level and source (such as WARN · intake), its time, its message, and "Until T+t s" when it covers a span, then "Markers come from fixed rules (config/report.toml) and state what the log shows; they do not name a cause." With none selected it says "Select a marker above the tracks to jump to it.", or "No rule fired in this match."

items.title: Readout
items.text:
One row per slot: the slot and its role, supply current (A), temperature (°C) and a temperature status:

Status Temperature OK Below temp_warn_c WARN At or above temp_warn_c FAULT At or above temp_fault_c (the row is highlighted)

With no cursor the heading reads MATCH MAXIMA · HOTTEST FIRST and the rows are each slot's match maximum, hottest first. With a cursor it reads AT T+t S, with the match phase, and the rows are the values at that moment. A slot that doesn't log a value reads "not logged".

items.title: OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE
items.text:
OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE opens the match's wpilog in AdvantageScope on the laptop running serve. A static export has no button, only the downloads. The result says "Opened file in AdvantageScope." and, when there are hoots, the folder to add them from with File › Insert log. A hoot whose end is missing (the robot lost power while writing it) is marked INCOMPLETE. If it fails: "AdvantageScope did not open:" and the reason. See Open a match in AdvantageScope and [advantagescope] in report.toml.

Under it, a download link for each raw log: ⇩ wpilog, or ⇩ hoot · and the bus. "No raw logs are recorded for this match." when there are none. A static export made with --no-raw lists each log's lake hash instead: "Raw logs not included in this export. Their lake hashes:".

items.title: Empty and error states
items.text:
State What Replay shows The lake has no imported logs No Replay data: "The lake holds no imported logs yet:" and the lake folder, the import command (flashpoint ingest --lake "<lake>" <folder>), a link to "Import logs by hand", how many files were quarantined if any, and Open Setup (served). The link reads "Open Setup: n problems to fix" when Setup has problems Logs, but none is a match No Replay data: "Replay lists only competition matches, identified from FMS data in the log or a match-style log file name. The lake's n sessions are practice, pit or other logs that are not a competition match." and a link to History, which counts their motor usage Matches, but no Replay data yet No Replay data: "n matches are waiting for Replay data. On the laptop that holds the lake, run:" flashpoint report A linked match isn't built The match key, "Replay data for this match is not built." and "Build it with flashpoint report --match <key>" (a static export says "This export does not include it."). The raw logs are still listed A match with no aligned samples "label · no aligned samples" and the reason: no wpilog to align the hoots to; no robot file for the robot code's project in that season (with Open Setup > Draft robot); or no device data could be aligned. Only the raw logs are available

serve builds missing Replay data when it starts, so the third state is usually seen in a static export, or while a build runs.

items.title: Shared on the network
items.text: Opened from another computer (flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0), Replay works the same except OPEN IN ADVANTAGESCOPE: in its place it says "Open in AdvantageScope is only available on the machine running Flashpoint. Use the downloads below." With --host 0.0.0.0 that is true on the laptop itself too. The downloads still work. COPY LINK can't reach the clipboard on a plain http:// address from another computer: it still reads COPIED, so copy the address bar instead. See flashpoint serve.

items.title: View: Setup
items.text: Setup shows what flashpoint doctor checks, with a button for the problems Flashpoint can fix, and your whole configuration, which you can change here without editing files. It also drafts a robot file from an imported log. It needs flashpoint serve, and fixes and saves run only on the laptop running it.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
The band at the top has three tabs under SETUP: CHECKS, CONFIGURATION and DRAFT ROBOT. On the right it shows the configuration folder ("configuration folder"). Under the band, a line says whether this page can change anything:

  • "Fixes and saves run on this computer."
  • "Read-only: this app is shared on the network (or not opened on the computer running it). Run the commands shown on that computer."

The tab is in the address (#view=setup&tab=draft), so a link can open one. The SETUP tab in the navigation shows a ! badge, on every view, while the lake's backup is overdue (overdue_h in acquire.toml). The backup check on CHECKS says why.

items.title: CHECKS
items.text:
The first line counts the results, such as "1 problem, 2 warnings. The same checks as flashpoint doctor." ("No problems" when there are none). Then one line per check, with its name and message:

Mark Status ✓ OK ! Warning ✕ Problem. doctor exits 1 while any problem remains – Doesn't apply on this computer, such as the acquire service on macOS

A settings file that is still the copy bundled with Flashpoint is marked DEFAULT. The CLI reference lists every check.

A warning or problem shows how to fix it. For the problems Flashpoint can fix, that's a button:

Button What it does Asks for Create configuration Writes the config folder, as flashpoint init does TEAM (number) and LAKE FOLDER (empty: the default lake folder) Download owlet Downloads and verifies owlet, CTRE's hoot converter, for each hoot format the lake has (or the newest, before the first import) Set AdvantageScope path Sets path under [advantagescope] in report.toml ADVANTAGESCOPE PATH Install the acquire service Installs flashpoint acquire --watch as a background service (Linux and Windows) Start the acquire service Starts the installed service (Linux and Windows)

After a fix, the checks run again and the line under the count says what was done and which files changed, or "Not fixed:" and the reason. Anything without a button shows the command or page to use instead.

items.title: CONFIGURATION
items.text:
Every section shows the file it comes from. DEFAULT marks a file that ships with Flashpoint; saving it writes your own copy into the config folder. A file that doesn't load shows its error in place of its values.

Section File What you can change TEAM AND CONNECTION acquire.toml TEAM NUMBER, LAKE FOLDER, and ROBOT ADDRESSES (COMMA-SEPARATED; EMPTY: FROM THE TEAM). "Acquire tries:" lists the addresses in use APPEARANCE theme.toml The team name and colours (below) ROBOTS robots/*.toml Per robot file: its SLOTS (SLOT, BUS, MODEL, CAN ID, SUBSYSTEM, ROLE), BUSES (NAME (ROBOT CODE), HOOT BUS) and SIGNALS (folded, with its count). A line above them gives the season, project, and the counts THRESHOLDS report.toml and anomaly.toml Every key, grouped by table, such as [thresholds] or [baseline] UNITS units/units-seed.csv Every CTRE device the team owns, by serial

In a table, + ADD adds a row and ✕ removes one. A slot with no subsystem is marked UNNAMED; that's allowed, and you can name it later. With no robot file yet: "No robot files yet. Draft one from a log in the DRAFT ROBOT tab."

items.title: SAVE
items.text:
Each section has its own SAVE. A save:

  • is checked with the same rules as loading the file, and refused with the same message if something is wrong, such as two slots with the same CAN id, or a signal under a root the season doesn't have;
  • is refused if the file changed on disk since you opened it: "file changed on disk since it was loaded; reload and redo the edit";
  • keeps comments and the order of everything you didn't change, and puts the previous version in .backups/ in the config folder (the last 20 of each file);
  • never changes the lake.

After a save the section says "Saved file. Next:" and what to do for the change to take effect:

File Next acquire.toml "a running acquire service picks this up after a restart" A robot file "flashpoint derive" report.toml "flashpoint report" anomaly.toml "flashpoint detect" The units list "nothing until the next derive (flashpoint derive)" theme.toml "every view, on its next page load (reload the page)"

A refused save says "Not saved:" and the reason.

items.title: Team name and colours
items.text:
TEAM NAME AND COLOURS sets what the header shows and the app's colours (Set the team name and colours):

  • TEAM NAME (HEADER, AT MOST 40 CHARACTERS);
  • TEAM NUMBER (EMPTY: FROM ACQUIRE.TOML);
  • COLOURS: a preset palette, or "custom colours", which adds PRIMARY, BACKGROUND (EMPTY: DEFAULT) and WARNING (EMPTY: AUTOMATIC), each as #RRGGBB text with a colour picker beside it.

The preview box under them redraws in the chosen colours: a header, a small chart, text and a warning. The rest of the app keeps the saved colours until you save and reload. Under the preview:

  • "✓ Readable: every text shade has at least 4.5:1 contrast on every surface, and the warning colour stands apart from the primary.";
  • or "Not readable, so it can't be saved:" with each failure, and a button for each colour to change, USE PRIMARY or USE WARNING followed by the nearest colour that passes, which puts it in the field;
  • or "Enter each colour as #RRGGBB, such as #00A3E0." while a colour isn't valid.

If theme.toml doesn't load, the section shows the error and "The app uses the default colours and no name until this is fixed."

items.title: DRAFT ROBOT
items.text:
Use this for a new robot, for hoot-only logs, or after --no-robot-draft (your first import usually drafts the robot for you). See Set up a robot file.

  1. Pick an imported log in the list. Each entry is its match key (or file name) and how many hoots it has, or "no hoots".
  2. Press DRAFT FROM THIS LOG. Every CAN device in its hoots becomes a slot. The line above the table says how many devices, the season and project, whether serials came from a CAN inventory ("serials from the CAN inventory", or "no CAN inventory in this log (no serials)", CAN inventory) and whether bus names did ("bus names from the robot code", or "no bus names logged", CAN bus status).
  3. Check ROBOT ID, and fill in each slot's SUBSYSTEM and ROLE now or later. SLOT can be renamed; BUS, MODEL, CAN ID and SERIAL come from the log. ✕ drops a slot.
  4. Press SAVE ROBOT. Every slot needs an id: "Give every slot an id first: n slot(s) have none."

A saved draft rebuilds the lake in the background: "Saved file. Rebuilding the lake in the background; reload Replay when it finishes (a minute or two)." If a rebuild is already running: "A rebuild is already running on this lake; reload Replay when it finishes."

A log with no hoots can't be drafted from: "this session has no CAN devices to draft from (no hoot files)".

On an empty lake the tab says "No imported logs yet. Import one match first:", with the import command for this lake and computer, how many files were quarantined if any, and a link to "Import logs by hand".

items.title: Empty and error states
items.text: State What Setup shows The checks can't run "Could not run the checks:" and the error The configuration can't be read "Could not load the configuration:" and the error The sessions can't be listed "Could not list sessions:" and the error A section's file doesn't load Its error, in place of its values (a robot file: "This file does not load." when there's no message)

items.title: Shared on the network
items.text:
Fixes and saves run only when serve is bound to this machine (the default) and the page is opened on that machine. Otherwise, including on the laptop itself with flashpoint serve --host 0.0.0.0:

  • the read-only line shows under the band;
  • each check shows its command instead of a fix button;
  • the configuration's fields are greyed out, its tables are plain text, and there's no SAVE, + ADD or ✕;
  • the colour preview shows the saved colours only;
  • DRAFT FROM THIS LOG still shows the draft, but there's no SAVE ROBOT.

Run the commands on the laptop running serve. See flashpoint serve.

items.title: Robot side: what to log
items.text:
Flashpoint reads the logs your robot already writes. Most of what it can tell you depends on what robot code logs. The list below is ranked: start at the top, and stop wherever your team runs out of time. The first two rows are what most WPILib and Phoenix 6 robots already do.

The samples are Java only (WPILib and Phoenix 6). C++ and Python teams can log the same entries; the entry names and formats on each page are what Flashpoint reads.

# Add What Flashpoint gains Without it Sample 1 Phoenix 6 signal logging (hoots), and a check for a hoot after each match Per-motor current, voltage, velocity and CAN dropouts: Replay's motor tracks, History, and most anomaly findings No CTRE motor data at all SignalLoggerSetup.java 2 The WPILib DataLog, with Driver Station data Match identity (event and match number), match phases, and the clock that lines hoots up with the match. Hoots need it: a session with hoots but no wpilog gets no motor history Hoot-only sessions; ingest warns, and motors get no history SignalLoggerSetup.java 3 Status-signal rates of 50 Hz for current, voltage, velocity and temperature, set before optimizeBusUtilization() Current spikes and stalls are visible, and timed to 20 ms After the optimisation, signals you didn't set drop to 4 Hz; Replay notes which slots log current slower than 20 Hz SignalRates.java 4 Phoenix Pro on the motors Motor temperature in the hoot: thermal tracks, temperature limits and thermal findings No temperature; everything else still works (a license, not code) 5 Build info The robot code's project name, which picks the robot file when a season has two robots (practice and competition) With two robots in a season, matches go to robot "unknown" BuildInfo.java 6 The CAN inventory Each motor's serial number, so its history follows the physical motor through swaps History is kept per slot (CAN id), split at the swap dates in your robot file CanInventoryLogger.java 7 CAN bus status Bus utilisation and error counts per bus, per match phase, in CAN health Those columns read "not logged" CanBusStatusLogger.java 8 Battery voltage and the PDH Today, nothing: Flashpoint uses a battery proxy. Entry names on that page are planned, not read yet Nothing lost today; declare a proxy device in your robot file none yet 9 Free disk space on the roboRIO and its USB stick Logs keep being written all event A full disk stops hoots, and WPILib deletes old wpilogs to make room (a pit check, not code)

To watch CAN dropouts live during shake and drive tests, robot code also publishes running totals over NetworkTables: see Live CAN health.

items.title: The sample project
items.text:
examples/robot-java/ is a minimal WPILib robot project with every sample in src/main/java/frc/robot/flashpoint/. The samples are suggestions, not a library: copy the files you want into your robot project (same package, or change the package line) and adapt them. Each file says which WPILib and Phoenix 6 versions it was tested with, on a line at the top. Check them against your versions before an event.

Robot.java wires all of them in one place:

  @Override
  public void robotInit() {
    SignalLoggerSetup.start();
    BuildInfo.log();

    SignalRates.apply(frontLeftDrive, intakeRoller);

    CanInventoryLogger.start();
    canBusStatus = new CanBusStatusLogger("rio", "DriveTrain");

    canHealth.add("DriveTrain", frontLeftDrive, frontLeftDrive.getPosition());
    canHealth.add("DriveTrain", frontLeftEncoder, frontLeftEncoder.getPosition());
    canHealth.add("DriveTrain", pigeon, pigeon.getYaw());
    canHealth.add("rio", intakeRoller, intakeRoller.getVelocity());
    canHealth.addBus("rio");
    canHealth.addBus("DriveTrain");
  }

Order matters in two places: SignalLoggerSetup.start() goes first, because everything after it writes to the log it starts; and SignalRates.apply(...) goes after you configure your motors.

To check that the project compiles (JDK 17; the first run needs network access, or the WPILib installer's ~/wpilib/2026/maven):

cd examples/robot-java
./gradlew compileJava

items.title: What Flashpoint doesn't read yet
items.text:
Some fields the samples log are kept but not used yet:

  • the firmware field in the CAN inventory (#87);
  • fault signals in the hoots (#86);
  • battery voltage and total current, whatever their entry names (#6).

items.title: AdvantageKit
items.text: AdvantageKit logs are not tested on real logs yet. See AdvantageKit and the support matrix for what works today.

items.title: AdvantageKit
items.text: What Flashpoint reads from AdvantageKit logs, and what it doesn't yet. Not tested on real logs: everything here is built and tested on synthetic logs made from AdvantageKit's own entry names (v26), and no outside team's AdvantageKit log has been checked yet (#76).

items.title: What works
items.text:
• Match identity. AdvantageKit logs the driver station's FMS data under /DriverStation/ (EventName, MatchType, MatchNumber, ReplayNumber, AllianceStation). Flashpoint reads them as in-log FMS data when the log has no WPILib FMSInfo entries, taking the whole set from one place, never mixing the two.
  • The filename. AdvantageKit names its log akit_yy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss_<event>_<p|q|e><n>.wpilog. Flashpoint reads the event, match and start time from it, like a WPILib FRC_… name.
  • The hoots' names. If the wpilog gives no identity at all, the match comes from the hoots' filenames (GACMP_Q7_…), which CTRE's signal logger takes from the same FMS data.
  • Pairing with hoots. AdvantageKit doesn't write WPILib's systemTime entry. Flashpoint anchors the log to wall-clock time with /SystemStats/EpochTimeMicros instead, so the wpilog and its hoots form one session.

A lake imported with an earlier Flashpoint picks these up on the next derive, which reads the affected logs' metadata again once.

items.title: What doesn't, yet
items.text:
• Alignment is very low. Flashpoint lines a hoot up with the wpilog by a payload both logged (DriveState/Pose over NetworkTables) or by enable edges. AdvantageKit's CTRE swerve template publishes neither the way Flashpoint looks for them, so alignment falls back to wall-clock time, with very low confidence. Replay shows its low-alignment warning: check the timing of events against AdvantageScope.
